Ariel sat on the ground, still deeply puzzled. "I don't get it. I still can't feel anything from you."

"You need to sense him carefully," Ren instructed, walking over to his brother. "First, you will notice that your body is instinctively rejecting the attempt to sense him out of pure, primal survival instinct. Second, you have to consciously tell your body that it is okay to sense him."

Ariel closed his eyes, focusing on his internal pathways. He felt the biological fail-safe Ren mentioned and forced his mind to bypass it. When he finally connected to Fajar's frequency, his eyes snapped open in sheer awe.

"Enjoy the view from the top while you can, Fajar. I'll catch up to you in no time."

### Route 4 Prologue Part 6

Fajar leaned against the marble pillar of the sanctuary, a deeply amused smirk tugging at the corners of his mouth. "You know, Ren, before we lock in this new insertion, I feel obligated to remind you of your own track record. It actually took you three distinct attempts—three full temporal loops—before you finally stabilized and made it to this realm."

Ren froze, his analytical mind suddenly stalling as a cold sweat broke out on the back of his neck. "Fajar... please do not pull up the archives."

"Oh, I am absolutely pulling up the archives," Fajar chuckled, waving his hand. A massive, shimmering holographic screen materialized above them. "Let's review your first run. The 'Hostile Vanguard' route."

The projection flared to life, displaying a violently dramatic, heavily saturated sequence of events.

"In your first attempt," Fajar narrated, thoroughly enjoying himself, "your presence drastically shifted the canon narrative into a relentlessly edgy, hostile melodrama. Right after Issei was resurrected, Rias Gremory cornered you, aggressively warning you not to interfere in devil affairs. You defied her, naturally. After the church raid, you ended up severely hospitalized. Rias visited your hospital bed not to thank you, but to threaten you with absolute hostility, demanding you stay away from her peerage because you stubbornly refused a memory wipe."

The projection shifted, showing a sullen, brooding Ren chopping vegetables in the background of a lavish mansion.

"Ah, the familiar training camp," Fajar continued. "You weren't even invited. But because your oppressive, lonely aura was so pathetic, Issei and Asia begged Rias to let you tag along out of sheer sympathy. You joined them, but you were strictly relegated to menial chores and cooking—which was honestly far more humiliating than just staying home, even though you secretly utilized the heavy labor for your physical conditioning."

The projection reached its climax. A battle-damaged, furious Ren stood in the Underworld, radiating dark, unstable energy.

"And then came the Riser Phenex rating game," Fajar said, his smile widening. "You bypassed the canon entirely, forcefully tapping into the raw, unrefined power of the 'Harrowing Interstice' to beat Riser to an absolute, bloody pulp. And to top it all off... you executed a flawless *Sasuke Uchiha* departure."

The screen showed Ren turning his back on the Occult Research Club under a blood-red moon. Rias, Issei, and the rest of the peerage were crying, apologizing, and begging him to stay. Ren merely scoffed, defeated them all in a swift, tragic skirmish to sever his bonds, and walked into the darkness.

"It was essentially a walking Netorare, or NTR, genre," Fajar concluded as the projection faded. "Maximum angst, maximum melodrama, zero healthy communication."

Ren’s face had turned a brilliant, glowing shade of crimson. He covered his face with both hands, groaning in profound, soul-crushing embarrassment. Ariel, meanwhile, had collapsed onto the marble floor. He was clutching his stomach, tears streaming down his face as he howled with hysterical, booming laughter.

"The chores! The Sasuke walk!" Ariel gasped for air, pounding his fist against the floor. "Bro, you were an edgy anime protagonist from 2007! I can't breathe!"

"Shut up!" Ren snapped, peeking through his fingers. He let out a long, ragged sigh, desperately trying to salvage a shred of his dignity. "Fine. What about the second attempt? It couldn't have been that bad."

Fajar tapped the air, bringing up a second, much calmer projection. "The second run. The 'Enlightened Scholar' route. You were much calmer this time. You finally achieved a sage-like mindset, and the *Highschool DxD* narrative remained much more realistic and grounded. However..."

The hologram showed a serene-looking Ren sitting on a park bench, violently scribbling in a notebook while muttering furiously to himself.

"It still carried a deeply pathetic, sorrowful vibe," Fajar noted dryly. "You spent seventy percent of your time internally complaining about why Issei was surrounded by a massive, loving harem while you didn't get a single girl to look your way. Ultimately, you left Kuoh gracefully as a traveling scholar, promising to return once your multiversal studies were complete. The ORC spent the rest of the timeline deeply regretting that they hadn't paid more attention to the quiet, brilliant boy in the back of the class."

Ren dropped his hands, his stoic facade completely shattered by the sheer cringe of his past lives. "That is so incredibly embarrassing. And it is completely unfair! Why doesn't Ariel have any embarrassing multiversal records to broadcast?!"

"Actually, I completely agree with you," Fajar laughed, nodding toward Ariel, who was still wiping tears of mirth from his eyes. "Ariel's loops were remarkably straightforward. He only took two attempts to ascend, and there was virtually no difference between them. In both timelines, Ariel just completely ignored the plot, abandoned Kuoh Academy entirely, and locked himself in his Personal Training Dimension to punch mountains. Total, unadulterated muscle-brain behavior."

A sudden spark of realization flashed behind Ariel's eyes as the archived memories slotted back into his restored soul. He let out a massive sigh of relief, flexing his biceps. "Oh, thank the heavens. I was just a brawler. Pure, simple, and unproblematic. No Sasuke walks for me."

Before Ren could formulate a bitter retort, a blur of motion darted from behind one of the sanctuary's massive pillars.

"Aww! If my poor, edgy brother needs some love, his little sister is always here for him!"

A pair of slender arms wrapped tightly around Ren's neck from behind in a crushing, affectionate hug. Ren and Ariel both spun around, their eyes going wide.

Standing there was a girl radiating bright, cheerful, and utterly chaotic energy. It was Kala Sofia Veritas. She was the embodiment of chaotic good, a multiversal wildcard whose singular, unshakable drive was to ensure everyone's absolute happiness. She was infamous in their old syndicate for her obsession with "Fixing Tragedies"—hijacking narratives purely to save characters destined to perish, like completely derailing the *Suikoden V* timeline just to ensure Ferid and Arshtat survived. She completely rejected sad endings.

"Kala!" Ariel roared, sweeping the petite girl into a massive, bone-crushing bear hug.

Ren immediately joined the embrace, his embarrassment evaporating as genuine, emotional tears pricked his eyes. To see his sister here, whole and radiating life, was a miracle he hadn't dared to hope for. "You're actually here... we're all together."

"Of course she is here," Fajar smiled, his divine presence warming the hall. "I told you, Ren. I found the *entire* Veritas bloodline through your temporal anchor." Fajar gestured toward the grand staircase at the far end of the hall. "Look up."

Descending the marble steps with a calm, composed, and highly organized demeanor was their brother, Kairos Draco Veritas. He was holding a glowing, ethereal clipboard, checking off multiversal coordinates.

"I heard everything," Kairos said smoothly, offering his brothers a warm, confident smile. "And I already have the insertion coordinates, timeline synchronization, and dimensional tethers fully prepped for your *Highschool DxD* drop."

Ariel and Ren broke their hug with Kala, beaming at their brother.

"Kairos!" Ren called out, profound relief washing over him. "I remember back in the community days... you always said you didn't want to fight on the front lines. You wanted to sit in the highest realm, watch over everyone, and act as the multiversal administrator."

Fajar crossed his arms, letting out a genuine sigh of relief. "And let me tell you, I am incredibly glad he took the job. Managing infinite realities requires an absurd amount of paperwork. Having Kairos handle the administrative burdens has taken a massive weight off my shoulders."

"Someone has to keep you all from breaking the space-time continuum," Kairos replied, tapping his ethereal clipboard with a smirk.

"Speaking of breaking things," Kala chimed in, turning her chaotic, sparkling eyes back to Ren. She threw her arms around him again, weaponizing his earlier embarrassment. "Ren, really, if you're feeling that lonely and want to bathe with your sister every day, you just have to say so!" She leaned in, dropping her voice to a theatrical, soft whisper. "You can even sleep under the same blanket with me every night so you don't have to be jealous of Issei's harem."

Ren’s face, which had just returned to a normal human shade, instantly ignited back into a blinding, atomic red. He stared at the ceiling, letting out a long, defeated sigh. "I give up. My dignity is permanently dead."

Ariel, completely failing to read the bizarre, teasing nature of the joke, slammed his fist against his chest. "Hey, that sounds like a great idea! I'll join in too! There's no need to be ashamed, Ren! We can all sleep in a giant pile! Let's forge an unbreakable bond between siblings!"

Ren slowly turned his head to stare at Ariel, utterly appalled by the sheer density of his muscle-brained brother.

Kala giggled, her chaotic energy practically vibrating the air around her. "Anyway! It was already decided with Kairos and Fajar before you guys woke up. I'm going to be joining your drop into Kuoh Town. And I am officially shifting the genre."

Ren rubbed his temples, a comedic, throbbing headache already forming. "What a pain. You're going to turn a supernatural war into a comedic chaos route, aren't you?" He paused, looking at his sister's beaming face, and finally let out a soft, resigned sigh. "But... maybe a comedic route could actually be fun for once."

"Exactly!" Ariel grinned, cracking his knuckles. "And Kala, whenever you need to break the plot, just call me. I'll smash whatever obstacles get in your way, just like the old days."

"It's a deal!" Kala cheered. She pulled up a holographic interface from her wrist. "But I'm not dropping in with you at the start. I'm setting my spawn point for *after* Issei is resurrected as a Devil. You two muscle-heads can enjoy your serious, gritty grinding time in the prologue. But the second I touch down... the genre completely changes to comedy!"

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 1 Sub Section 1

The world stabilized with a soft, atmospheric hum.

Ren opened his eyes, expecting the cramped, functional layout of his old Kuoh apartment. Instead, his gaze met high vaulted ceilings, polished hardwood floors, and the warm, ambient light filtering through the large bay windows of a spacious two-story suburban house. Beside him, Ariel flexed his fingers, taking a deep, appreciative breath of the crisp morning air.

"Not a bad spawn point," Ariel chuckled, looking around the furnished living room.

Ren walked over to the mahogany entryway table, where a neat stack of official identification documents, family registries, and residential deeds was laid out. He picked up the heavy paper file, his dark eyes scanning the text.

"Fajar and Kairos handled the administrative integration flawlessly," Ren noted, handing a document to Ariel. "According to the municipal records, we are officially the **Veritas Siblings**—a family of four. Kairos is listed as our legal guardian and eldest brother, currently managing off-site academic research. You and I are enrolled at Kuoh Academy as second-year students. And Kala is registered as our younger sister, currently completing an overseas exchange program until her scheduled transfer."

Hanging on the wardrobe doors in the adjacent hallway were two pristine, freshly ironed Kuoh Academy male uniforms.

"Time to put on the armor," Ariel grinned, throwing off his casual jacket and slipping into the black-and-white school uniform. He adjusted the collar, his broad shoulders straining slightly against the fabric even with his physical stats suppressed.

Ren put on his own uniform, buttoning it up methodically. But as he adjusted his cuffs, the local temporal memories of this reality forcefully synchronized with his conscious mind. A sudden, sharp throbbing ignited behind his temples. Ren pressed two fingers to his forehead, letting out a long, pained groan.

"What's wrong, tactician?" Ariel asked, slinging his school bag over one shoulder. "Insertion shock?"

"No," Ren sighed, his voice dripping with pure exhaustion as they opened the front door and stepped out onto the sunlit streets of Kuoh Town. "My local identity status just updated. I am officially classified as a member of Kuoh Academy's infamous **Perverted Quartet**. My social standing is in the absolute gutter."

Ren turned to his brother, squinting through a fresh wave of second-hand embarrassment. "Which brings me to an urgent question. How in the world did someone with your athletic build, heroic aura, and straightforward personality get dragged into their orbit in this timeline? What is your backstory with them?"

Ariel burst into a loud, booming laugh, rubbing the back of his neck. "Oh, that! It was a total misunderstanding at first, man! A few weeks ago, I was sitting on a park bench during lunch, reading the newest issue of *Weekly Shonen Jump*. Matsuda and Motohama saw the cover—it was a big color spread of a major battle arc—and sat down next to me to talk about it."

Ariel shrugged, a bright, naive smile on his face. "I thought they were just fellow battle-manga enthusiasts bonding over hype fights and martial arts scaling! But then Motohama started flipping to the color pin-ups and ecchi fanservice pages, and Issei joined in, making these crazy, wildly perverted comments. That's when I realized: *'Oh, wow, these guys are absolute degenerates!'*"

Ren stared at him. "And you didn't immediately walk away?"

"Why would I?" Ariel asked, completely genuinely. "Sure, they're lecherous muscle-brains who think with their hormones ninety-nine percent of the time, but deep down, they're honest, loyal, and good people! They don't pretend to be fake polite aristocrats. Issei would take a bullet for his friends. A real man doesn't cut ties with his bros just because they have trashy hobbies!"

Ren rubbed his temples again. "Your muscle-brained optimism is going to be the death of me."

As they approached the massive iron gates of Kuoh Academy, both brothers felt the faint, thrumming pulse of Fajar's dimensional limiter humming deep within their cores. Their raw physical output—their physical strength, speed, and durability—alongside their active Qi discharge, was strictly capped to Level 1 mortal human bounds. They couldn't shatter mountains or tear open dimensions with a punch.

*However*, their sensory capabilities remained entirely unhindered. Ren’s Observation Haki and sensory overclocking, alongside Ariel’s intention sensing, were as sharp and expansive as ever. Even if they walked through the campus completely blindfolded, every heartbeat, kinetic shift, and whispered murmur across the entire school ground was instantly mapped in their minds.

And right now, Ren's hyper-tuned hearing was picking up every single piece of gossip from the female students lined up along the walkway.

"Eww, look... it's Ren," a female student whispered to her friend, turning her face away in disgust. "One of those gross creeps from the perverted quartet."

"I know, right?" her friend sneered softly. "He always has that cold, moody look. He's probably thinking of something utterly filthy."

Ren’s headache spiked violently. But as they took a few more steps, the public perception narrative took an absurd, completely unexpected left turn.

"Wait... but look who he's walking with!" another girl gasped, her voice suddenly dripping with deep, melodramatic pity. "It's Ariel-kun!"

"Oh, poor Ariel-kun!" a third girl whimpered, clutching her hands over her heart. "He's so handsome, athletic, and sweet! He's literally like a sun! It is such a heartbreaking tragedy..."

"I know!" her friend agreed, tears practically welling in her eyes. "He only has to hang out with those awful perverts because Ren is his brother! Ariel-kun is just being a dutiful, loving, and loyal brother who refuses to abandon his family, even when his brother is a social outcast! He's suffering in silence to protect him! It's so noble!"

Ren froze dead in his tracks. He turned his head slowly, looking at Ariel, who was cheerfully waving to a group of third-year girls with a blinding, movie-star smile, causing three of them to swoon against the school fence.

"Are you kidding me?" Ren hissed, his voice trembling with comedic outrage. "The local reality narrative turned me into the designated black-sheep scapegoat, while framing *you* as a tragic, saintly martyr who is forced to endure the perverted trio out of brotherly sacrifice?!"

"Hey, don't look at me!" Ariel grinned, throwing his arm around Ren's shoulder in a heavy, affectionate headlock. "I didn't write the school's headcanon! But hey, perks of being the supportive brother, right?"

"Get off me," Ren muttered, shoving Ariel's arm away, though he couldn't stop the faint, amused twitch on his lips.

They pushed through the double doors leading into the main courtyard, where three familiar figures were gathered near the giant sakura tree.

Issei Hyoudou was slouched against the trunk, sipping a box of sweet strawberry milk. Beside him, Matsuda was aggressively flipping through a crumpled magazine, while Motohama pushed up his thick glasses, analyzing something on his phone with the intensity of a top-tier tactical general.

"Yo! Ren! Ariel!" Issei called out, noticing them first and raising his hand in a lazy wave.

Matsuda instantly dropped his magazine, his eyes bulging as he stomped over to them. "Ren, you traitorous bastard! Why are you walking next to a guy who looks like he stepped out of a high-budget sports anime?!"

"Statistically speaking," Motohama added, marching up beside Matsuda and tapping his phone screen, "Ariel’s sheer physical charisma and athletic reputation briefly elevate our group's social baseline by approximately four point two percent! However, his radiant presence simultaneously draws a dangerous volume of female attention to our covert perimeter, completely ruining our stealth operations!"

Ariel stepped forward, delivering a massive, hearty slap to Issei's back that sent the Pawn stumbling forward, coughing on his strawberry milk.

"Good morning, boys!" Ariel boomed, his energy completely shattering the gloomy atmosphere of the perverted trio. "Ready for another glorious day of youth?!"

"Ariel, man, you're gonna break my spine one of these days!" Issei wheezed, wiping his mouth and grinning. He then looked at Ren, noticing his stoic, incredibly annoyed expression. "What's with you, Ren? You look like you swallowed a lemon."

"I am currently contemplating the statistical probability of surviving high school without dying of sheer mental fatigue," Ren replied flatly, folding his arms.

"Ah, don't worry about it!" Matsuda laughed, throwing his arm around Issei's neck. "We've got big plans today, boys! The track team is practicing on the south field during fourth period!"

As Matsuda and Motohama launched into a passionate, highly detailed breakdown of their upcoming, doomed reconnaissance mission, Ren stood quietly beside Ariel. He watched Issei’s bright, completely innocent laughter—the laughter of a normal, foolish high school boy who had no idea that a spear of light, a crimson magic circle, and the entire supernatural underworld were silently waiting for him in the shadows of the coming weeks.

Ren exchanged a quick, subtle glance with Ariel. The Level 1 grinding era had officially begun.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 1 Sub Section 2

Matsuda slammed his hands down on Issei’s desk, completely abandoning their previous conversation. "Forget the track team! I have acquired critical, time-sensitive intel. There is a structural compromise near the Kendo club dojo. A loose ventilation grate behind the equipment shed gives a direct, unobstructed line of sight into the girls' changing area!"

Motohama pushed his glasses up the bridge of his nose, the lenses gleaming ominously. "My calculations confirm a ninety-eight percent probability of a flawless view. However, the terrain is treacherous. The perimeter is heavily guarded by third-year enforcers. We need a flawless infiltration route." Both of them turned in unison, staring at Ren with desperate, pleading eyes. "Ren. We need your tactical genius."

Ren blinked slowly, his expression entirely devoid of emotion. He leaned back in his chair, crossed his arms, and let out a long, heavy sigh. "No. I am entirely uninterested in this endeavor. Once the final bell rings, I am going to put my head on this desk and sleep until the janitor kicks me out."

Complete, stunned silence fell over the group. Issei dropped his strawberry milk. Matsuda's jaw unhinged. Motohama’s glasses slid down his nose.

"Sick... he must be sick!" Issei yelled, suddenly waving his hands frantically around Ren's face. "Matsuda, check his temperature! Is it a fever? A concussion? Did a stray baseball hit you in the head on the way to school?!"

"I am in perfect physical health, Issei," Ren replied, slapping Issei's hand away with a dull glare. "I am simply, fundamentally, completely uninterested in crawling through the dirt to look at high school girls."

"But you don't understand!" Matsuda dropped to his knees, clasping his hands together in absolute despair. "The maintenance staff is doing perimeter checks! That loose grate is going to be welded shut by tomorrow morning! This is a once-in-a-lifetime, limited-edition event! If we don't strike today, the promised land will be sealed forever!"

"Please, oh great tactician!" Motohama begged, bowing so low his forehead practically touched the floor. "Guide us through the shadows!"

Ren pinched the bridge of his nose, the comedic headache returning with a vengeance. He looked over at Ariel, who was leaning against the classroom doorway, highly amused by the entire spectacle. "Ariel, please. If I have to endure this soul-crushing pain, you are coming with me. Help me escort these absolute fools so they don't get themselves expelled on day one."

Ariel chuckled, walking over and clapping a heavy hand onto Ren’s shoulder. "Come on, bro, it's just a simple escort mission. Look on the bright side! You managed to show the entire school how drastically you changed your life before, right? You can absolutely do it again here. In fact, think about the sheer sensation of blowing this entire school's mind when the 'creepy pervert' suddenly transforms into a stoic, untouchable sigma male. That's a legendary character arc that even I won't get a chance to experience!"

Ren paused. The sheer narrative potential of completely shattering the school's perception of him began to outweigh his immediate annoyance. A faint smirk finally touched his lips. "You know... you make an incredibly compelling point. Thank you, Ariel." Ren stood up, his eyes narrowing as he shifted into full operational mode. "Alright, you degenerates. If we are doing this, we follow my exact route. One mistake, and you're on your own."

The trio erupted into muffled, triumphant cheers.

Thirty minutes later, the infiltration was well underway. Moving with terrifying, ghost-like precision, Ren led the trio through the blind spots of the courtyard, utilizing the shadows of the old school building, the timing of the changing bells, and the exact patrol routes of the disciplinary committee.

"I remember this," Ariel whispered, effortlessly crouching behind a row of thick hedges alongside Ren, completely ignoring the trio who were army-crawling through the dirt ahead of them. "You always admired tactical espionage games. You're literally treating this like a *Metal Gear* stealth sequence."

"If you treat every mundane task as a life-or-death tactical simulation, your baseline operational awareness never degrades," Ren muttered back, not breaking his focus.

Ahead of them, Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama finally reached the holy grail—the rusted ventilation grate. They pressed their faces against the metal slats, giggling like maniacs as they enjoyed their illicit view.

Ariel and Ren, completely uninterested, remained seated behind the thick hedges, relaxing in the shade. However, within seconds, the invisible, atmospheric pulse of Ariel’s Observation Haki rippled outward. His eyes widened slightly.

"Ren," Ariel whispered, his tone dropping its jovial edge. "I'm picking up hostile intent. Sharp spikes of suspicion coming from inside the dojo."

Ren closed his eyes, his hyper-tuned senses sweeping the area. "Confirmed. Two girls near the lockers just noticed a shadow moving across the grate. Their breathing patterns just shifted to an aggressive, alert state."

Ariel leaned forward, his voice a harsh, urgent hiss. "Hey! Issei! Matsuda! Fall back right now! They're suspicious. Hide in the brush!"

"Are you crazy?!" Matsuda hissed back, not taking his eyes off the grate. "We're at the climax! The captain is taking off her chest guard!"

"Statistically, if we stop now, we lose all momentum!" Motohama added, completely blinded by his own degenerate excitement. "We don't hear anything! Your senses are just paranoid!"

Ariel groaned, looking back at his brother. "Ren, what's the play here? We can't let them get caught."

"Give up," Ren said flatly, his eyes still closed. "You cannot save a fool from his own folly. We cannot forcefully pull them away without making noise and exposing ourselves."

Suddenly, Ariel’s Haki flared again, this time violently. "Wait. It's not just the dojo. I've got multiple hostile signatures rapidly converging on our location from the eastern corridor and the southern courtyard. They're surrounding the perimeter!" Ariel turned back to the grate. "Guys, I am entirely serious! It is getting extremely dangerous! Abort the mission!"

"Never!" Issei whispered furiously, tears of joy streaming down his face. "This is peak youth!"

Ariel gritted his teeth and turned to grab Ren's shoulder to initiate an emergency tactical retreat. "Ren, we have to—"

Ariel grasped empty air. He blinked, staring at the empty patch of grass beside him. Ren was completely, utterly gone. There was no sound, no displaced air, no rustling of leaves. The tactician had simply evaporated the moment he confirmed the perimeter was breached.

"That treacherous, brilliant bastard," Ariel muttered in sheer awe.

A split second later, the heavy wooden doors of the dojo smashed open. A legion of furious, bamboo-sword-wielding Kendo girls poured out into the alleyway, their eyes burning with righteous fury.

Ariel didn't hesitate. With a burst of suppressed but explosive athletic power, he bolted from the hedges, scaled the sheer brick wall of the equipment shed in three rapid, parkour-style leaps, vaulted over the rusted roof, and vanished into the tree line just as the death squad descended upon the perverted trio.

"Found them! The perverted trio!" a third-year girl screamed. "No mercy!"

"Wait! No! It's a misunderstanding!" Issei shrieked, raising his hands defensively.

The alleyway erupted into a chaotic, comedic symphony of brutal thwacks, yelps of pain, and desperate apologies as the Kendo club unleashed hell upon Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama.

Ten minutes later, the battered, bruised, and highly traumatized trio limped back toward the main courtyard. Their uniforms were covered in dirt and footprints, and Matsuda had a massive, comical bump throbbing on the top of his head.

"I can't believe it..." Issei groaned, rubbing a painful welt on his cheek. "Where did Ariel and Ren go? They were right behind us!"

"Tactical abandonment," Motohama whimpered, his glasses cracked right down the middle. "They utilized us as biological meat shields to facilitate their own escape. Ren's tactical genius is terrifying."

As they stumbled past the old, decaying architecture of the Occult Research Club building, Issei paused. The setting sun cast a deep, golden-orange hue over the campus. Issei looked up toward the second-floor window.

Standing there, bathed in the twilight, was a girl with hair the color of spilled crimson, her piercing blue eyes looking down at him with an enigmatic, unreadable expression. For a brief, surreal moment, the pain in Issei's body vanished, replaced by a strange, magnetic pull that echoed deep within his chest.

"Woah..." Issei breathed, completely mesmerized.

Matsuda grabbed Issei's collar, yanking him forward. "Don't even look, man. That's Rias Gremory. The absolute top of the food chain. She is in a completely different dimension from trash like us."

Issei stumbled after his friends, but he couldn't stop himself from glancing back one last time at the crimson-haired girl in the window, completely unaware of the gears of destiny slowly turning around him.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 1 Sub Section 3

Ariel dropped silently from the corrugated roof of a nearby convenience store, landing in a crouch within the shadow of a narrow alleyway two blocks away from Kuoh Academy. He stood up, dusting off his uniform, and looked around in genuine confusion. He had utilized maximum parkour efficiency to escape the Kendo club's wrath, expecting Ren to be miles ahead of him.

"Where did he go?" Ariel muttered, scanning the bustling pedestrian street.

"I have been standing right here for the past three minutes," a flat, monotone voice spoke from the shadows directly behind a nearby vending machine.

Ariel jumped, spinning around to see Ren leaning casually against the brick wall, sipping a canned black coffee. "Bro! How did you beat me here? You don't even have my vertical leap stats!"

"I didn't outrun you, Ariel," Ren sighed, crushing the empty can and tossing it flawlessly into a recycling bin. "While you were violently vaulting over rooftops and drawing all the kinetic attention, I simply utilized the chaotic distraction you created. I dropped my heart rate, merged with the visual blind spots of the Kendo club members, and literally just walked out the front gates at a leisurely pace. It is basic tactical espionage maneuvering."

Ariel stared at him, shaking his head. "You are an absolute menace. Anyway, we need to shift gears. The timeline is moving fast. The incident with Raynare is going to happen soon, and since Fajar heavily capped our internal energy and physical output, we need actual, physical gear."

Ren nodded in agreement. "There's a massive, multi-level discount superstore down the street. It has everything from groceries to industrial hardware. We go there."

Thirty minutes later, the brothers were navigating the chaotic, neon-lit aisles of a store that heavily resembled a Don Quijote. The sheer volume of random merchandise was staggering, but Ren moved with cold, calculating purpose. He completely bypassed the cheap, flashy display weapons and headed straight for the professional hunting and outdoor survival section.

After meticulously testing the balance and carbon-steel composition of several blades, Ren selected three professional-grade tactical knives with matte-black finishes to prevent light reflection. He then moved to the sporting goods section, grabbing a heavy-duty, reinforced extendable steel pole.

"A collapsible staff," Ren muttered, testing the locking mechanism with a swift flick of his wrist. "Perfect for mid-range spatial control."

Ariel watched him, his arms crossed. "I was planning to just use my bare hands to cave in the skulls of any Fallen Angels we run into, but while we're here..." Ariel reached into a nearby display case of 'novelty biker accessories' and pulled out a pair of solid, heavy-duty brass knuckles. He slipped them onto his fists, testing the weight with a few sharp jabs in the air. "Yeah. These will add some nice blunt-force trauma to my striking kinetic energy."

They moved to the apparel section to finalize their loadouts. Ren opted for a tactical, dark-grey cloak set that offered maximum concealment for his throwing knives and obscured his physical silhouette in low-light environments. Ariel, completely rejecting stealth, chose a highly elastic, lightweight combat-athletic set consisting of reinforced track pants and a compression shirt, prioritizing absolute, unhindered joint mobility and explosive movement.

With their bags packed and their wallets significantly lighter, the brothers began the trek back toward their new suburban home.

As they crossed the bridge over the local river, Ariel paused, resting his hand on the railing. Just a few meters down the walkway, standing against the sunset, was Issei Hyoudou. He was blushing furiously, frantically bowing to a beautiful girl with long, dark hair and an innocent, nervous smile.

"There it is," Ariel whispered. "Yuma Amano. Raynare in her human disguise."

Ren didn't even turn his head to look. His sensory perception had already mapped her exact bio-rhythm and the faint, suppressed scent of light magic emanating from her core. "We do not need to pay attention to them. The canon narrative is securely locked in. We know exactly where this goes."

They continued walking, leaving Issei to his doomed twilight confession.

"I've been thinking about Fajar's Route 0," Ren said quietly, his eyes narrowing with competitive determination. "Fajar dismantled a Fallen Angel cadre and an elite Exorcist with nothing but biomechanics and borrowed weapons. I want to break his legendary streak. When the time comes, I am going to beat Raynare to an absolute pulp using nothing but pure, unadulterated human tactical superiority."

Ariel grinned, his blood already pumping at the thought of a genuine fight. "If we're going to pull that off with Level 1 stats, we need to optimize our muscle memory immediately. You know the rule, Ren. Sparring is always the fastest way to train when time is short. Our minds remember our god-tier techniques, but these physical bodies need to be forcefully synchronized with our reaction times."

Ren dropped his shopping bags on the grass as they reached an abandoned, fenced-off construction lot near their neighborhood. "Agreed. How do you want to run this? Old times?"

"Unarmed combat sparring first," Ariel declared, tossing his own bags aside and dropping into a loose, bouncing boxer's stance. "No weapons. Just raw, kinetic application. Let's see how much force we can generate with these restricted mortal shells."

Ren didn't answer with words. He simply shifted his weight, his presence instantly vanishing as he slipped into the blind spot of Ariel's peripheral vision.

The silence of the evening was instantly shattered by the sharp, whip-like crack of flesh hitting flesh. Ariel deflected a lightning-fast palm strike aimed at his throat, countering with a sweeping roundhouse kick that carried enough raw, perfected biomechanical torque to snap a normal man's femur. Ren ducked under the heavy blow by a millimeter, using the momentum to sweep Ariel's planted leg.

For the next hour, the abandoned lot became an intensive, hyper-focused battleground. Dust kicked up into the twilight air as the two brothers traded hundreds of calculated, brutal strikes, completely ignoring the fatigue of their mortal bodies as they forcefully forged their Level 1 stats into absolute, lethal perfection.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 2 Sub Section 1

The morning commute to Kuoh Academy was completely derailed by the sight of Issei Hyoudou strutting down the sidewalk, an obnoxiously proud grin plastered on his face as he held hands with the beautiful, dark-haired Yuma Amano.

Matsuda was practically tearing his own hair out, dropping his school bag in the dirt. "This is a glitch in reality! A biological impossibility! How does a degenerate like him get a cute girlfriend before me?!"

Motohama was frantically furiously typing on his phone. "My calculations are completely shattered! The probability of Issei achieving romantic success without divine intervention was zero point zero zero one percent!"

Ariel walked up and slapped Issei on the back, nearly knocking the wind out of him. "Congratulations, man! Youth is in full bloom! Treat her right!"

Ren, walking calmly beside his brother, adjusted his collar and gave Issei a curt, polite nod. "Congratulations on your first relationship, Issei. I hope you enjoy your time together."

Matsuda and Motohama froze, their heads snapping toward Ren with absolute, betrayed horror.

"Ren... what the hell is wrong with you?!" Matsuda shrieked, pointing an accusing finger at him. "Ariel, I get! He's a shining beacon of athletic positivity! But you? You're one of us! You're supposed to be biting your lip and crying tears of blood in agonizing jealousy!"

"I have simply matured past the need for petty envy," Ren replied with a perfectly deadpan expression, completely ignoring the fact that in his past loop, he had absolutely cried tears of blood over this exact scenario.

Yuma giggled, leaning against Issei's arm. "You have such funny friends, Issei-kun! Well, I have to get to my school now. See you on our date later, my darling!"

As Yuma waved and jogged away, Issei waved back like a lovesick puppy, while Matsuda and Motohama dramatically collapsed onto the pavement in utter despair.

Ariel and Ren left the crying duo behind, walking a few paces behind Issei as they approached the school gates.

"So," Ariel muttered under his breath, not changing his cheerful expression. "Did your hyper-senses pick up the little white-haired mascot tailing them yesterday afternoon?"

"Koneko Toujou," Ren affirmed quietly. "Yes. She was completely focused on tracking Issei's movements and mapping his routine. The Occult Research Club is actively monitoring his threat level."

Meanwhile, inside the decaying architecture of the old school building, the Occult Research Club was holding a morning briefing.

Koneko sat on one of the plush leather sofas, quietly nibbling on a chocolate biscuit. Rias Gremory sat behind her grand desk, while Akeno Himejima poured tea and Yuuto Kiba stood near the window.

"Your surveillance was accurate, Buchou," Koneko reported in her usual flat, emotionless tone. "The Fallen Angel known as Raynare has initiated contact under the alias Yuma Amano. She is clearly targeting Issei Hyoudou. This confirms he is harboring a Sacred Gear."

"Excellent work, Koneko," Rias smiled, resting her chin on her intertwined fingers. "We will keep a close eye on him. Did anything else happen during your patrol?"

Koneko stopped chewing. A rare, faint flicker of confusion crossed her golden eyes. "There is... an anomaly. I successfully tailed Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama to the Kendo dojo. However, the Veritas brothers were with them. When the perimeter was breached..." Koneko paused, looking directly at Rias. "Ariel scaled a three-story vertical brick wall in under two seconds using raw physical momentum. And Ren... he simply vanished. He stepped into a blind spot and my tracking lost him completely. Neither of them used a trace of demonic or magical energy. They just disappeared."

Kiba blinked in surprise. "Normal humans outmaneuvered you, Koneko?"

"Ara, ara," Akeno chuckled, placing a teacup on Rias's desk. "It seems our school's perverted quartet has some hidden talents."

Rias’s eyes narrowed slightly, a spark of genuine intrigue flashing in her blue eyes. "Keep observing Issei for now. But if the Veritas brothers show any more anomalies, I want to know immediately."

Hours later, the final bell rang, echoing across the campus.

Issei practically vaulted over his desk, violently shoving his textbooks into his bag with chaotic speed.

"Hey, where's the fire?" Matsuda asked, leaning back in his chair. "We have a recon mission at the tennis courts!"

Issei slung his bag over his shoulder, striking a ridiculously arrogant pose. "Sorry, losers! I've got a date with my beautiful girlfriend! You boys have fun in the dirt! Hurry up and get a girlfriend so you can be on my level!"

With a booming, victorious laugh, Issei bolted out the classroom door.

Matsuda and Motohama sat in stunned, crushing silence, their egos thoroughly shattered by Issei's brutal parting words.

Ren calmly stood up, picking up his bag. "Well, I am leaving as well."

Matsuda slammed his hands on his desk, tears streaming down his face. "How can you be so calm, Ren?! The hierarchy is broken! Issei is ascending to the heavens while we rot in the abyss!"

"Calm down," Ren sighed, adjusting his bag. "Let him have his fleeting moment of arrogance. We will systematically interrogate him tomorrow after his ego crashes back to reality. Let's go, Ariel."

"Right behind you!" Ariel laughed, waving to the crying duo as he followed Ren out of the classroom.

An hour later, the abandoned construction lot echoed with the sharp, lethal sound of clashing steel.

Ren moved like a phantom, his dark cloak swirling around him as he seamlessly transitioned from his extendable steel pole to the matte-black tactical knife in his left hand. He thrust the blade toward Ariel’s ribcage with terrifying, calculated precision.

Ariel didn't flinch. Relying entirely on his restricted Level 1 stats and peerless biomechanical mastery, he parried the knife strike with his brass knuckles, the metal sparking violently as they collided. Ariel immediately countered with a devastating hook aimed at Ren's jaw, forcing the tactician to flip backward to avoid the concussive force.

The sun set over Kuoh Town, casting long shadows over the lot as the two brothers pushed their mortal bodies to the absolute limit, preparing for the inevitable clash of light and blood.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 2 Sub Section 2

The morning commute to Kuoh Academy was a familiar, agonizing loop of degenerate melodrama. Matsuda and Motohama were practically dragging their feet across the pavement, loudly lamenting the gross injustice of the universe while Issei eagerly babbled about his upcoming second date with Yuma.

However, amidst the usual chaos, there was a glaring anomaly. Ren was not staring stoically ahead or rubbing his temples in annoyance. Instead, his eyes were locked onto his smartphone, his thumb rapidly tapping and dragging across the screen with intense, focused precision.

"Whoa, hold on," Issei said, pausing his monologue and leaning over Ren’s shoulder. "Are you playing a game? Wait... is that chess?"

Matsuda blinked, momentarily forgetting his heartbreak. "Ren? Playing a mobile game? I thought your only hobbies were sighing at us and looking like you're plotting a murder."

"I have always played chess after school," Ren replied smoothly, not taking his eyes off the digital board as he castled his King. "I merely preferred the physical desktop environment. I am currently adapting my processing speed to the mobile interface."

Issei laughed, throwing his hands behind his head. "Man, you're such a nerd sometimes! You should be looking around! The morning commute is prime time for spotting cute girls from other schools!"

As the trio resumed their loud, hormone-fueled debate over which school uniform was superior, Ren subtly shifted closer to Ariel.

"I am not just playing chess," Ren whispered, his eyes still glued to the screen while he effortlessly sidestepped a cracked paving stone. "I am forcefully splitting my cognitive load. I am actively mapping a fifty-meter sensory perimeter, tracking the bio-rhythms of every pedestrian, and manually regulating the circulation of my internal energy, all while calculating variations on the board."

Ariel’s eyes widened, a massive, brilliant grin splitting his face. He whispered back, his voice vibrating with sheer athletic hype. "Bro, twenty-four-hour continuous passive training? That is absolute genius! If you're doing cognitive-sensory overload, I need to start maximizing my physical downtime immediately!"

Without missing a beat, Ariel dropped into a deep, walking lunge, perfectly keeping pace with the group while bringing his back knee a millimeter from the concrete with every step. The perverted trio didn't even notice, too caught up in their own delusions.

When the lunch bell rang, Issei immediately grabbed his bag, fully intending to sprint off campus to buy a specific brand of juice Yuma had mentioned liking. He made it exactly two steps before Ren, completely engrossed in his phone, casually stuck his foot out and shifted his shoulder, forming an immovable human barricade in the doorway.

"Hey! Move, Ren!" Issei complained, trying to push past him.

Ariel suddenly dropped from the top of the doorframe, where he had been doing suspended pull-ups on the molding, landing with a heavy thud right next to Ren. "Sorry, Issei! You have an appointment!"

Matsuda and Motohama instantly flanked the doorway, their expressions twisting into terrifying, jealous sneers.

"The interrogation begins now, you lucky bastard!" Matsuda roared, dragging a protesting Issei back to his desk by his collar.

While Matsuda and Motohama aggressively interrogated Issei about every single detail of his first date—down to the exact millimeter of distance between their hands—Ariel dropped to the floor, seamlessly transitioning into a set of rapid, one-armed clapping push-ups.

Ren sat at his desk, his thumb hovering over his phone. The digital board was highly complex. His Queen, Bishop, and Knight had successfully infiltrated the enemy King's corner.

*I have a discovered check,* Ren’s mind raced, his tactical senses firing. *If I move the Knight, the Bishop checks the King, and I win the enemy Queen for free. It is the objectively correct, safe move. But... the geometry is too perfect. I can force a checkmate in five moves. I must pursue perfection.*

Ren dragged his Knight to a hyper-aggressive square, sacrificing a pawn to trap the King, fully expecting the opponent to move their Rook to block. Instead, the opponent made a completely irrational, defensive retreat, pulling their own Knight back to an awkward, terrible square that somehow perfectly covered the checkmate square.

"WHAT?!" Ren shouted, his voice echoing over Matsuda's screaming.

Ariel popped up from his push-ups, immediately jogging over to Ren's desk. He leaned in, his eyes scanning the digital board. Despite not being a dedicated chess player, centuries of watching Ren formulate war strategies and play multiversal grandmasters had given Ariel a terrifyingly sharp eye for the game.

Ariel burst into a booming laugh. "Oh, bro, you got greedy! You completely tunnel-visioned on the forced mate and missed the Knight retreat! You could have taken the Queen for free on the previous turn!"

"I know!" Ren hissed, his thumb hovering frantically over the screen as the time clock ticked down to twenty seconds. "Now the position is completely equalized! It's an endgame scramble!"

Sweat formed on Ren's brow. He was deeply sour about missing the brilliant checkmate, his frustration clouding his usually flawless emotional control. With ten seconds left, the opponent's King advanced, attacking Ren's Rook.

Ren’s eyes darted across the screen. *If I push my pawn sideways, it attacks their Rook. If they take the pawn, I have a discovered attack on their Rook. If they ignore it, I take the pawn with my Rook! It's a brilliant counter-trap!*

Ren aggressively slammed his thumb on the screen, pushing the pawn.

Instantly, the opponent slid their Rook across the back rank, checking Ren's completely exposed King. Ren had no pieces to block. He was forced to move his King away, abandoning his own Rook to be captured for free. The entire position collapsed in a single move.

Ren stared at the screen in pure disbelief. He slowly pressed the resign button, dropped the phone on his desk, and aggressively slapped his own forehead with the palm of his hand.

Ariel had to cover his mouth to stop himself from howling with laughter. "You were too tilted, man! You were so frustrated that you didn't get the beautiful win earlier that you completely refused to calculate the draw, and you missed a basic back-rank check!"

"You are entirely correct," Ren groaned, rubbing his eyes. "I let my ego dictate my calculations. I learned my lesson. If the universe hands you a free Queen, you take the Queen. You do not overcomplicate the execution."

By the time the afternoon sun began to dip toward the horizon, Matsuda and Motohama had dragged Issei—who was trying to leave early again—to the chain-link fence surrounding the outdoor tennis courts.

"Observe, gentlemen," Motohama whispered intensely, his glasses gleaming. "The second-year girls' tennis club. The wind conditions are optimal. When they execute a high-velocity overhead serve, the kinetic momentum guarantees a ninety-four percent chance of a skirt flip!"

"This is the promised land!" Issei wept, completely forgetting about his date for a split second as the trio pressed their faces against the wire mesh.

A few feet away, entirely separated from the degenerate behavior, Ariel was doing deep, slow, weighted squats, using a massive, abandoned concrete block he had found behind the equipment shed. Ren was sitting in the shade of a large oak tree, his eyes locked onto his phone screen while his Observation Haki flawlessly mapped the trajectory of every tennis ball on the court.

However, the trio's aggressive, heavy breathing had an immediate, adverse effect. The female students noticed the blatant peeping. Disgusted and deeply uncomfortable, the girls began playing terribly, keeping their knees locked and their movements rigid to prevent their skirts from lifting even a millimeter.

"No! They're compromising their form to protect their modesty!" Matsuda cried out in agony.

Under the tree, the sound of a loud, sharp slap echoed. Ariel dropped the concrete block, which hit the dirt with a heavy thud, and jogged over to his brother.

Ren was staring at his phone, his hand clamped over his face in sheer, unadulterated shame.

Ariel peered at the screen and immediately started laughing again. "Bro! That was a completely free Queen! Your opponent literally just blundered their Queen right next to your pawn, and you... you pushed your pawn forward to block it?!"

"I won the game anyway!" Ren defended himself, his face slightly red. "The positional advantage was overwhelming! But yes... I completely missed the capture."

"How do you miss a free Queen?!" Ariel chuckled, wiping a tear from his eye.

"Because I am accustomed to playing high-level Rapid and Blitz time controls!" Ren complained, gesturing to the screen. "My rating on those formats is extremely high. I am used to playing against rational opponents who do not make catastrophic, nonsensical blunders! This is my first time playing one-minute Bullet chess on a new account! The opponent made a move so incredibly stupid that my brain completely filtered it out as a possibility!"

Ariel crossed his arms, smirking down at the tactician. "So what you're saying is, your expectations are too high. You're so used to fighting gods that you forgot how to fight a Level 1 goblin."

Ren paused, his annoyance fading into a sharp realization. He looked at the digital chessboard, then at Ariel. "You are exactly right. It is a fundamental flaw in my current methodology. It is genuinely important to play against lower-rated opponents occasionally. If I cannot recognize and punish a basic mistake because I am over-anticipating a masterstroke, I will fail in the field."

"Hey! I gotta go!" Issei suddenly yelled from the fence, checking his watch. "Yuma is waiting for me at the park! See you losers tomorrow!" Issei bolted off into the sunset, leaving Matsuda and Motohama to weep by the tennis courts alone.

Ren slipped his phone into his pocket and stood up, dusting off his uniform. "Let him go. His time is running short."

"Agreed," Ariel said, cracking his knuckles, his jovial demeanor instantly shifting into a hyper-focused, lethal calm. "Let's leave these fools to their crying. The sun is setting. It's time for us to spar."

The Friday morning walk to Kuoh Academy was an absolute masterclass in psychological torture for two specific second-year students.

Issei walked at the front of the group, strutting with his hands behind his head, practically floating on an invisible cloud of romantic bliss. Beside him, Yuma Amano held his elbow, giggling sweetly at every terrible joke he made.

"Issei-kun, you're so funny!" Yuma squeaked, leaning her head against his shoulder. "I'm so excited for our big date at the park tomorrow evening!"

"Ehehe! Me too, Yuma-chan!" Issei beamed, his face beet red. "I've been counting down the hours!"

Right behind them, Matsuda and Motohama looked like two hollowed-out husks wandering toward their execution. Matsuda was literally chewing on the corner of his own handkerchief, leaving damp bite marks in the fabric, while Motohama was furiously scratching his fingernails against a nearby concrete wall.

"Look at him," Matsuda wept, his voice cracking with unbearable anguish. "Look at his stupid, smiling face! He's holding hands with a girl! In broad daylight!"

"My soul is disintegrating," Motohama whimpered, his glasses sliding down his nose as tears blurred his vision. "The contrast between his romantic success and our absolute solitude is generating a localized field of pure despair. Why him?! Why not us?!"

Ren walked a few paces behind the suffering duo, his phone held loosely in his right hand. Beside him, Ariel was executing crisp, low-impact calf raises with every single step, casually maintaining his physical conditioning while enjoying the melodrama.

"Have a wonderful day at school, Issei-kun!" Yuma called out as they reached the intersection leading to her academy. She gave Issei a quick, delicate wave and blew him a kiss before jogging away.

Issei stood on the sidewalk for three full minutes, waving like a brainless mannequin, before turning back to the group with a smug, insufferable grin. "Alright, boys! Let me hear it! How jealous are you on a scale of one to ten?!"

"A hundred!" Matsuda roared, yanking Issei into a headlock. "A billion!"

As the trio dissolved into their usual chaotic scuffle down the main walkway, Ariel’s eyes flickered. The invisible, atmospheric pulse of his Observation Haki expanded across the campus, filtering through the dense waves of student chatter lined up along the iron gates.

Ariel leaned in close to Ren, his lips barely moving as he whispered. "Bro... your chess match yesterday completely broke the school's social radar. Listen to these rumors."

Across the courtyard, a group of second-year girls whispered frantically behind their notebooks.

*"Did you hear?! Ren was playing competitive mobile chess yesterday during break!"*
*"Wait, chess?! Since when does anyone play chess at Kuoh besides President Rias and Student Council President Sona?!"*
*"Is he secretly an elite intellectual?! Was he just pretending to be a pervert this whole time to fit in with Hyoudou and the others?!"*
*"No way... maybe he was never a real pervert at all! Maybe he was just acting as a cover for his brother Ariel-kun!"*
*"Wait, didn't he completely ignore the girls' tennis team upskirts yesterday?! He sat under a tree and didn't look once!"*
*"Do you think he's heartbroken because Hyoudou got a girlfriend first?!"*
*"Or maybe... he's undergoing a dramatic, silent redemption arc?!"*

Ariel grinned, nudging Ren's elbow. "Did your hyper-senses catch all of that, tactician? The entire school is currently debating whether you're a secret grandmaster, a tragic brother, or a reformed villain."

Ren kept his gaze fixed straight ahead, his expression entirely stoic. "I caught every single frequency. The human mind’s innate compulsion to construct elaborate, dramatic narratives out of mundane actions never fails to amuse me."

"So you really didn't plan any of this?" Ariel asked, chuckling softly. "You didn't intend to build this whole mysterious, cool aura?"

"I merely ceased method-acting as a brainless degenerate," Ren replied, adjusting the strap of his school bag. "I reverted to my original, baseline state. I stopped caring about the mob's superficial opinions. I play chess because it sharpens my tactical geometry. If they interpret basic rationality as an enigmatic transformation, that is their analytical failure, not my concern."

Ariel slapped Ren’s shoulder with a bright, appreciative laugh. "Still, bro... you gotta admit. Playing chess under a tree, ignoring upskirts, and letting the entire student body think you're some stoic, untouchable genius? That's cool as hell."

A rare, faint smirk touched the corner of Ren’s lips. "I will confess... it is significantly more agreeable than having water balloons thrown at my head."

By the time the final afternoon bell rang, the atmosphere in the Year 2 classroom reached a boiling point.

Issei didn't even wait for the teacher to leave the room. He shoved his books into his bag, leaped over two desks, and struck a victorious pose at the door. "Later, losers! I've gotta go buy some fresh clothes and get haircut prep for my big date tomorrow! Try not to die of loneliness while I'm gone!"

Before Matsuda or Motohama could hurl their erasers at him, Issei vanished down the hallway with a loud, triumphant laugh.

Matsuda slammed his head violently against his wooden desk. *THUD.* "I can't take it anymore! A date at the park on a Saturday evening! What are they going to do when the sun goes down?! What if they go to a cafe?! What if they hold hands on a bench?!"

"My mind is generating explicit, highly detailed visual simulations of their romantic progression," Motohama groaned, clutching his temples as he slumped in his chair. "The psychological agony is fatal. If I cannot verify what happens on this date, I will not survive the weekend!"

Motohama turned to Ariel, bowing deeply with profound reverence. "Ariel-san... you are an absolute tactical genius! We must assemble disguise kits and binocular gear immediately!"

"To the discount store!" Matsuda roared, yanking Motohama by the arm as they bolted out of the classroom like two men possessed.

Ariel watched them sprint down the hallway, rubbing the back of his neck with a sheepish grin. But as the sound of their footsteps faded, Ren quietly walked up beside him, his dark eyes locked onto his brother.

Ariel’s smile faltered slightly. "Uh... Ren? You're giving me your 'you just compromised the operational parameters' look. Did I mess up the timeline by blurting that out?"

Ren adjusted his collar, a sharp, deeply calculating glint flashing in his eyes. "On the contrary, Ariel. That was a stroke of unadulterated, accidental genius."

Ariel’s eyes lit up with immediate realization, a proud grin returning to his face. "Yes! That way, Matsuda and Motohama don't get left behind as forgotten side characters! We keep the entire squad together from day one!"

"Precisely," Ren agreed. "However... it is a double-edged sword."

Ariel’s smile sobered. "Because they're normal humans."

"Because exposing untrained, baseline mortals to supernatural violence, blood, and demonic magic can permanently shatter their mental stability," Ren noted coldly. ### Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 1

The Saturday evening air was crisp as the sun began its slow descent over Kuoh Town's central plaza. Hidden behind a thick row of manicured hedges, Matsuda and Motohama were completely decked out in the most suspiciously conspicuous espionage gear imaginable—khaki trench coats, fedoras, and dark sunglasses. They were pressed belly-down in the dirt, their eyes practically glued to the lenses of their heavy-duty binoculars.

A few feet away, entirely ignoring the concept of stealth, Ariel and Ren were sitting comfortably on a park bench. Ariel was happily devouring a massive strawberry crepe, while Ren was slowly sipping a canned black coffee, his eyes closed in absolute, serene relaxation.

"Target is currently purchasing a strawberry ice cream cone," Matsuda hissed, furiously twisting the focus dial on his binoculars. "Wait. He just handed it to her. She is taking a bite. He is taking a bite of the exact same cone! Indirect kiss confirmed! My internal organs are hemorrhaging from the stress!"

Motohama was frantically scribbling in a tiny notebook. "The spatial proximity between their shoulders has decreased to less than two centimeters. The probability of hand-holding within the next five minutes has skyrocketed to ninety-nine point9 percent! This is a catastrophic development for our social hierarchy!"

Matsuda tore his eyes away from the binoculars for a fraction of a second to glare at the brothers on the bench. "How are you two so calm?! Issei is literally ascending to a higher plane of existence, and you're just sitting there eating pastries!"

"Because we are currently executing a highly calculated recovery phase," Ren replied smoothly, not opening his eyes.

"Exactly," Ariel mumbled through a mouthful of crepe cream. "You guys didn't see us last night. We were doing intensive, full-contact biomechanical optimization training until four in the morning. Our muscles need glycogen replenishment and zero-stress downtime before we exert any sudden kinetic force."

"You guys talk like you're preparing for a war zone!" Motohama complained, adjusting his glasses. "We are witnessing the death of our youth! Wait—target lost! The crowd shifted! Where did they go?! I lost visual!"

"Dammit! Did they go into the cinema?" Matsuda panicked, scanning the plaza wildly.

Ren took another slow sip of his coffee. He didn't even turn his head. "They are currently fifty meters to your direct left, standing in front of the accessory boutique. Her heart rate has elevated slightly as she points at a silver necklace."

Matsuda and Motohama immediately whipped their binoculars to the left.

"He's right!" Matsuda gasped. "How the hell did you know that?! You didn't even look!"

Ten minutes later, the crowd surged around a street performer, and the duo lost Issei again.

"Visual lost! Did they enter the underground mall?!" Motohama sweated.

Ariel licked some whipped cream off his thumb. "Nah, they just walked past the crepe stand. They're heading toward the central park fountain. About a hundred and twenty meters north."

Matsuda stared at Ariel in sheer, terrified awe. "Are you guys mutants? Do you have satellite tracking devices implanted in your brains? You're literally psychic!"

"We simply possess superior situational awareness," Ren stated flatly, finally opening his eyes as the golden hour faded into the deep, bruised purple of twilight. His relaxed demeanor vanished instantly, replaced by a cold, razor-sharp focus. He crushed the empty coffee can in his grip. "The ambient temperature is dropping. The pedestrian density in the central park is rapidly decreasing. Ariel."

Ariel swallowed the last of his crepe, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand. His jovial smile disappeared. "Yeah. I feel it too. The atmosphere just got incredibly heavy."

Matsuda and Motohama, oblivious to the shift in the air, scrambled out from the bushes and sprinted toward the treeline overlooking the central fountain. Ariel and Ren followed closely behind, moving with complete, silent fluidity.

When they reached the clearing, Issei and Yuma were standing alone by the bubbling water of the fountain. The sky was entirely dark now, illuminated only by the flickering park lamps.

"They're stopping," Matsuda whispered, his hands trembling as he held up the binoculars. "The date is over. Is he going to kiss her? I can't watch! I can't look away!"

From across the clearing, Yuma's sweet, innocent voice drifted over the rushing water, but her words made the blood freeze in Matsuda and Motohama's veins.

"Will you die for me?"

Issei recoiled, a nervous, confused laugh escaping his lips. "H-Huh? What did you say, Yuma-chan?"

The air pressure violently inverted. A suffocating, malevolent aura erupted from the girl. Yuma's cute, civilian clothes dissolved into a flurry of dark, leathery feathers, replacing her attire with a highly revealing, bondage-style dominatrix outfit. From her back, two massive, pitch-black wings tore through the fabric of reality, extending outward with a terrifying gust of wind.

Matsuda dropped his binoculars. They hit the pavement with a sharp crack.

Motohama fell backward onto the grass, his mouth opening and closing in absolute, soundless terror. "W-W-What... what is that? Wings? A monster? Cosplay? What is happening?!"

"A Fallen Angel," Ren whispered, his voice completely devoid of fear.

At the center of the fountain, Raynare raised her hand to the sky. A blinding, lethal spear of pure, condensed light materialized in her grasp. The sheer ambient heat radiating from the weapon caused the fountain water to hiss and evaporate.

"Goodbye, Issei Hyoudou," Raynare sneered, pulling her arm back to impale the terrified boy through the heart.

*Clank. Splash.*

Raynare blinked. A crushed, half-empty can of black coffee had just bounced directly off the center of her forehead, spilling a few cold drops onto her nose before splashing into the fountain.

She froze, her majestic, lethal execution completely derailed by sheer, unadulterated disrespect. She slowly turned her head toward the treeline, her eyes burning with furious, divine wrath. "Who dares—"

She didn't get to finish the sentence.

Ariel didn't just run; he exploded from the treeline. Channeling every single ounce of his restricted Level 1 physical stats into pure, forward kinetic momentum, he closed the distance in a fraction of a second. Before Raynare could even adjust her grip on the light spear, Ariel launched his entire body weight forward, driving a devastating, rugby-style shoulder tackle directly into her midsection.

The impact was thunderous. The sheer biomechanical force lifted the Fallen Angel completely off her feet, knocking the wind from her lungs with a sickening gasp. The spear of light slipped from her fingers, shattering into harmless, glowing particles as it hit the concrete.

"A-Ariel?!" Issei shrieked, falling backward onto the ground, completely unable to process why his athletic best friend had just materialized out of thin air to tackle a winged monster.

Back in the treeline, Matsuda was furiously pulling his own hair, screaming in sheer, reality-breaking hysteria. "He tackled it! Ariel just tackled a winged demon! What is happening to our youth?!"

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 2

Raynare scrambled backward across the wet concrete of the fountain, her eyes wide with a mixture of absolute shock and rising, divine fury. She raised her hand, desperately attempting to manifest a second spear of light, but her magical circulation was instantly violently interrupted.

Ariel did not give her a single microsecond to breathe. Moving with the terrifying, relentless efficiency of an apex predator, he stepped inside her guard, slipping perfectly under a panicked, sweeping backhand. He pivoted on his heel, driving a devastating right hook into her floating ribs, followed instantly by a lightning-fast left uppercut that snapped her head back with a sharp, echoing *crack*.

"What are you?!" Raynare shrieked, blindly flapping her massive, pitch-black wings in a desperate attempt to create spatial distance. She launched a jagged, unrefined bolt of pure light magic directly at Ariel's chest.

Ariel didn't even block. He simply tilted his torso two degrees to the left. The lethal magic scorched the air a millimeter past his shoulder, completely missing its target. "I'm just a high school student with an excellent workout routine!" Ariel boomed, stepping forward again and delivering a brutal, spinning back-kick that sent the Fallen Angel skidding across the pavement.

Before Raynare could recover her footing, a shadow detached itself from the treeline.

Ren sprinted across the clearing, his dark grey tactical cloak billowing behind him like the wings of a phantom. He drew his matte-black combat knife, the blade completely absorbing the dim park lighting. Raynare swung her wing forward like a massive, bladed shield to crush the incoming mortal, but Ren’s eyes tracked the kinetic telegraphing of her shoulder muscles flawlessly.

He slid beneath the sweeping wing, his knees scraping the concrete, and slashed upward in a flawless, crescent arc. The carbon-steel blade tore through the leathery feathers and the fabric of her dominatrix attire, leaving a stinging, shallow line of crimson across her thigh.

"Filthy human!" Raynare roared, summoning a short-sword of light and slashing wildly at Ren’s neck.

Ren casually deflected the trajectory of her glowing blade with the reinforced spine of his tactical knife, parrying the divine weapon with simple, irrefutable physics. He stepped smoothly into her blind spot, delivering a rapid sequence of four precise cuts to her triceps, hamstrings, and the connective tissue of her wings.

To the untrained eye, Ariel and Ren looked like unstoppable, mythological gods of war utterly dismantling a demon. However, the internal reality of the battlefield was incredibly restrictive. Fajar’s dimensional limiter was operating at maximum capacity, aggressively suppressing their physical and energetic output. Ariel's flawless, biomechanically perfect strikes—which should have instantly shattered Raynare’s ribcage into dust—merely bruised her ribs and knocked the wind out of her. Ren’s hyper-accurate slashes—aimed perfectly at major arteries and tendons—were forcefully dulled by his capped mortal strength, resulting in dozens of superficial, stinging paper-cuts that infuriated the Fallen Angel far more than they actually damaged her.

Yet, despite their damage being capped at Level 1, the battle was almost insultingly easy. Raynare's combat technique was sloppy, arrogant, and entirely reliant on overwhelming magical firepower. Against two multiversal grandmasters who could read her intentions before her brain even fired the electrical signals to her muscles, she could not land a single hit.

Issei Hyoudou was still sitting in the wet grass near the fountain, his jaw unhinged, his eyes bulging out of his skull. The romantic, terrifying climax of his first date had completely transformed into an incomprehensible martial arts spectacle.

"A-Ariel? Ren?!" Issei stammered, frantically gripping his own hair. "Since when do you guys know kung fu?! Why does Ren have a military knife?! What is happening to my life?!"

In the bushes fifty meters away, the situation had deteriorated into pure, unfiltered hysteria.

Matsuda had his binoculars pressed so hard against his face that they were leaving deep, red circular indents on his skin. "Motohama! Motohama, tell me I am hallucinating! Ren just parried a laser sword with a pocket knife! Ariel is boxing a winged demon!"

Motohama was rocking back and forth in the dirt, clutching his notebook to his chest like a protective shield, his mind completely failing to process the mathematical impossibility of the scene. "The laws of physics are crumbling! Ariel’s evasion rate is statistically impossible for a baseline human! Ren’s stealth parameters are exceeding modern military stealth technology! We have been mocking highly trained covert operatives this entire time!"

"Are we going to die?!" Matsuda wept, aggressively shaking Motohama by the collar. "Is this why they didn't care about the tennis club upskirts?! Because they fight monsters in their free time?!"

Back in the center of the fountain clearing, Ren ducked under another frantic, sweeping light spear, slicing a neat line across the back of Raynare's calf before smoothly retreating to stand beside his brother.

"She is incredibly slow," Ren noted calmly, twirling the knife effortlessly in his left hand.

"And her guard is practically non-existent," Ariel laughed, bouncing lightly on the balls of his feet, entirely unharmed and barely breaking a sweat. "But man, Fajar really nerfed our output. I hit her with a hook that should have launched her into the stratosphere, and she just stumbled!"

"It is sufficient for our current tactical objectives," Ren murmured, his eyes narrowing as he expanded his Observation Haki across the park's perimeter.

Ariel threw a quick, sharp jab into the air to keep his muscles warm. "Hey, tactician. If we completely humiliate her and she runs away, Issei doesn't die. If Issei doesn't die, Rias Gremory never resurrects him as a devil. Don't we absolutely need him to die to trigger the primary canon timeline?"

"We do," Ren affirmed softly, his gaze remaining locked on the furious, bleeding Fallen Angel in front of them. "But we do not need to purposefully throw the fight. My hyper-senses have already confirmed the presence of three additional hostile signatures. They are currently concealed in the atmospheric shadows atop the gothic church spire two kilometers away, and they are rapidly descending upon our location."

Ariel’s grin widened into a fierce, battle-hungry smirk. "Ah. Raynare's backup. Kalawarner, Mittelt, and Dohnaseek. So the script fixes itself."

"Precisely," Ren said, adjusting his grip on the matte-black blade. "We simply have to survive the escalation."

"I WILL SLAUGHTER YOU BOTH!" Raynare screamed, her voice distorting into an unholy, echoing screech that shattered the glass of the nearby park lamps. Her entire body erupted with a blinding, violently unstable aura of raw, destructive light magic. She raised both hands to the sky, preparing to unleash an indiscriminate, omnidirectional bombardment that would vaporize the entire plaza—including Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama.

But before she could bring her hands down, the sky above the park completely fractured.

Three massive, heavy impacts shook the concrete as three new figures descended from the pitch-black clouds, landing directly between Raynare and the Veritas brothers.

A towering man in a fedora and trench coat with a condescending sneer. A tall, voluptuous woman in an elegant blue dress with cold, calculating eyes. And a petite, blonde girl in a gothic lolita outfit, twirling a parasol with a sadistic giggle. From the backs of all three new arrivals, majestic, pitch-black wings unfurled into the night air.

"Really, Raynare?" Dohnaseek sneered, pushing the brim of his fedora up with a gloved finger as he looked down at the battered, humiliated girl. "You're being pushed to the brink of a magical meltdown by two baseline human teenagers? How utterly pathetic."

"Shut up!" Raynare hissed, clutching her bleeding arm. "They aren't normal! They move like phantoms!"

Mittelt giggled, pointing her parasol directly at Ren. "Ooh, but they are cute! Can I play with them before we kill the Sacred Gear host?"

Ren simply raised his knife, settling into a flawless, low-profile defensive stance, while Ariel cracked his knuckles, the metal of his brass knuckles gleaming in the ambient light of the Fallen Angels' auras. The true battle of Route 4 had officially begun.
