### Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 3

Mittelt giggled, her high-pitched laughter echoing across the park as she twirled her gothic parasol. "I call dibs! Let's see how you boys squeal!"

With a burst of dark feathers, the blonde Fallen Angel vanished from her spot, reappearing directly above Ariel and Ren with her parasol extended like a deadly lance. She expected to skewer them effortlessly, anticipating the satisfying crunch of mortal bones.

Instead, she hit empty air.

Ariel didn't even look up; he simply pivoted on his heel, his body fluidly sidestepping the lethal thrust by a mere millimeter. As Mittelt's momentum carried her downward, Ariel raised his knee, burying it squarely into her ribs with a sickening thud. Before she could even gasp, Ren spun from her blind spot, his matte-black tactical knife flashing in the dim light.

For a fraction of a second, Ren’s muscle memory overrode his suppressed mortal state. He instinctively channeled his multiversal mastery, embedding a microscopic fragment of his indomitable will—his Haki—into the very edge of the blade. The steel effortlessly bypassed Mittelt's innate magical defense, slicing a deep, agonizing gash across her forearm.

Mittelt shrieked, tumbling backward onto the concrete and clutching her bleeding arm. "Agh! What the hell?! That actually hurts! These aren't normal humans!"

Ariel glanced at Ren, a hint of annoyance crossing his face. "Bro, how did you get through her magical skin so easily? My strikes are just giving her deep bruises!"

"I remembered to embed my will into the kinetic trajectory of the blade," Ren replied, his eyes never leaving the enemy.

Ariel groaned, slapping his forehead. "Damn it! I completely forgot we could still use conceptual intent even with the limiters! I’ve just been using raw physical torque!"

Hovering above the fountain, Dohnaseek’s arrogant sneer completely evaporated. He stared at Mittelt's bleeding arm, his eyes narrowing as he re-evaluated the situation. "Impossible. They are moving with zero magical fluctuation, yet their biomechanical efficiency is flawless. Kalawarner! Stop playing around!"

Kalawarner, floating with her arms crossed, clicked her tongue in annoyance. "Fine. But if they move like ghosts, I will simply target the dead weight."

She summoned a spear of light, its core burning with intense, azure heat, and hurled it not at Ren, but directly at Issei, who was still sitting frozen in the grass.

Ren’s hyper-senses screamed. His tactical mind processed the variables in a microsecond: *If I let Issei die here, the plot proceeds flawlessly. But if I stand perfectly still and watch him get impaled when I have already demonstrated peerless speed, my cover as a loyal friend is entirely blown.*

"Tch. What a pain," Ren muttered. He lunged forward, throwing his entire body weight into Issei.

"W-Waah!" Issei screamed as Ren tackled him into the dirt. The light spear detonated exactly where Issei’s chest had been a split second prior, blasting a scorching crater into the earth and showering them with superheated dirt.

Kalawarner smirked, her eyes glinting with cruel realization. "Look at that, Dohnaseek. The phantoms are shackled. They are protecting the weaklings. Target their friends!"

The battlefield dynamics shifted violently. Raynare, her pride shattered and her eyes burning with pure malice, joined Mittelt. The two of them descended upon Ren and Issei in a flurry of sweeping light swords and explosive magical bursts.

Ren was instantly forced onto the defensive. He extended his steel pole, using it to parry the divine weapons while simultaneously dragging a hyperventilating Issei across the grass. The tactical genius was genuinely struggling now; he could easily dodge every strike, but shielding a stationary, screaming civilian required him to absorb graze damage. His dark cloak scorched at the edges as he deflected a blast meant for Issei's head.

"Ren! Why are you doing this?!" Issei bawled, clutching his head as explosive light shattered a nearby bench. "You're going to die because of me!"

"Shut up and keep your head down!" Ren barked, his calm demeanor finally cracking under the sheer annoyance of the escort mission.

Simultaneously, Dohnaseek and Kalawarner locked their sights on the thick bushes where Matsuda and Motohama were hiding.

"Found the other rats," Dohnaseek laughed, forming two massive spears of light.

Matsuda and Motohama shrieked in absolute, existential terror, clutching each other as the sky illuminated above them. "Our youth is over! We're dying as virgins!" Matsuda sobbed hysterically.

Before the spears could leave the Fallen Angels' hands, a blur of motion intercepted the trajectory. Ariel sprinted at breakneck speed, throwing himself directly between the bushes and the descending angels. He raised his arms, crossing them in a dense, defensive guard.

The explosive shockwaves of the light spears slammed into Ariel’s forearms. Without the ability to use his internal energy to harden his skin, the searing heat burned his forearms, and the concussive force sent several jagged cuts across his cheek and shoulders. Blood trickled down Ariel's chin, but he didn't yield a single inch, planting his feet firmly into the soil.

"A-Ariel-san is bleeding!" Motohama wept, watching his athletic friend take the brunt of the divine wrath. "He is sacrificing his perfect physique for our miserable lives!"

"Is that all you've got?!" Ariel roared at Dohnaseek, grinning through the pain, his adrenaline spiking as he protected the crying duo.

Suddenly, amidst the deafening explosions and frantic screaming, a calm, entirely out-of-place sound echoed through the clearing.

*Clap. Clap. Clap.*

Everyone—the Fallen Angels, the terrified mortals, and the Veritas brothers—froze.

Stepping out from behind an oak tree on the edge of the park was a completely ordinary-looking high school student. He had messy hair, a relaxed posture, and wore a standard Kuoh Academy uniform. He carried absolutely no magical aura, no demonic presence, and no angelic light. He was, by all sensory metrics, a baseline human.

But as Fajar walked onto the battlefield, the sheer, crushing weight of his absolute authority made the ambient air pressure physically drop.

Fajar chuckled, casually stuffing his hands into his pockets as he looked at Ariel's bruised arms and Ren's scorched cloak. "I thought you two just wanted to beat them up? Are you actively trying to break my legendary Route 0 streak?"

Ariel wiped the blood from his cheek, grinning widely. "Hey! We had it completely under control until they initiated AoE bombardment!"

Fajar nodded thoughtfully, pacing across the cracked concrete, completely ignoring Kalawarner’s readied spear. "I must admit, during my run, I was notoriously terrible at hostage rescue and civilian protection. By bringing the perverted trio into the crossfire, you’ve actually raised the difficulty modifier of this scenario significantly. It is quite an impressive flex."

Ren parried a residual spark of light from Mittelt and glared at Fajar. "What are you doing here? You explicitly stated you would not interfere with the early game grinding phase."

"I am here for scheduled maintenance," Fajar smiled warmly. "The designated date and time have arrived to remove your limiters. Honestly, if you hadn't dragged Matsuda and Motohama into this, the fight would have ended ten minutes ago and you would have moved on."

Fajar paused, looking around at the sheer, absolute chaos—Issei crying on the ground, Matsuda and Motohama praying to various deities in the bushes, and four highly confused, heavily armed winged demons hovering in the sky.

"However," Fajar's smile widened into a terrifyingly excited grin, "seeing how incredibly fun this chaotic escort mission looks... I think I will join the fight."

Above them, Dohnaseek blinked, his brain completely short-circuiting. "What... what is happening? Who is this child? What limiters?!"

In the dirt, Issei looked back and forth between Ren, Ariel, and the new arrival. "Ren... Ariel... do you know this guy? Why is he talking like this is a video game?!"

Motohama aggressively adjusted his cracked glasses from the bushes. "Difficulty modifiers?! Limiters?! What kind of secret society are we mixed up in?!"

Fajar merely laughed, cracking his neck as he stepped onto the frontline. The mortals and the Fallen Angels had absolutely no idea that the apex predator of the multiverse had just joined the server.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 4

Fajar stretched his neck, producing a series of sharp, echoing cracks that cut through the chaotic noise of the battlefield. While Ariel and Ren fought with a measured, tactical balance—preserving energy and analyzing variables—Fajar possessed an entirely different combat paradigm. He was hungry for blood. His movements were not just precise; they were fiercely, terrifyingly aggressive.

As he stepped fully into the clearing, Fajar began to circulate his internal energy. It was strictly capped at the human baseline, offering no superhuman physical enhancements, but Fajar didn't need enhanced stats. He seamlessly embedded his absolute, multiversal will into his strikes. Worse yet, he passively projected a monstrous, apex-predator aura. His opponents didn't realize it, but their subconscious minds were screaming in mortal terror, causing their magical defenses to involuntarily waver and break before Fajar even touched them, multiplying the kinetic damage they received tenfold.

Dohnaseek sneered, completely misreading the situation. "Another suicidal human! I'll impale you where you stand!" The towering Fallen Angel manifested a massive spear of light and thrust it directly at Fajar's chest.

Fajar charged straight forward, not breaking his stride. To Ariel and Ren, who could sense intent, it was an incredibly reckless maneuver. But Fajar’s sensory perception operated on an entirely different dimensional axis. He wasn't just reading intentions; his Advanced Observation Haki was allowing him to literally foresee the future, mapping out Dohnaseek's exact trajectory seconds before the muscles even twitched.

Fajar simply tilted his head, letting the searing heat of the light spear graze his cheek. In the exact same synchronized motion, Fajar dropped his center of gravity and executed a flawless *Renewal Recoilless Baekdu*.

By eliminating all wasted kinetic energy and applying absolute rotational torque, Fajar drove his knee directly into Dohnaseek’s solar plexus. The impact sounded like a cannon firing. Despite hitting a biologically superior entity, Fajar's embedded will and terrifying aura bypassed the Fallen Angel's durability entirely. Dohnaseek's eyes bulged, blood erupting from his mouth as his ribcage fractured.

Without giving the angel a microsecond to breathe, Fajar seized Dohnaseek's trench coat, pivoted his hips, and launched into a textbook *Ippon Seoi Nage*. Fajar threw the massive Fallen Angel over his shoulder with one arm, slamming him into the concrete with such catastrophic force that a spiderweb of cracks cratered the park plaza.

"One down," Fajar whispered, his eyes glinting with a sadistic thrill.

Ariel burst into laughter, bouncing on his heels as he turned his attention to Kalawarner. "Looks like the boss is warming up! My turn!" Ariel slipped under Kalawarner's frantic barrage of light magic, dismantling her guard with a brutal combination of liver blows and uppercuts that sent the elegant Fallen Angel staggering backward in sheer panic.

Fajar didn't linger on Dohnaseek. He pivoted and locked his sights on Raynare, who was still trying to recover from Ren's tactical cuts.

Seeing the human who had just effortlessly pulverized Dohnaseek charging at her, Raynare shrieked, blindly throwing horizontal arcs of light magic. Fajar closed the distance in a blur. He trapped her extended arm and unleashed a devastating barrage of Wing Chun chain punches directly to her sternum and face, mixing the rapid-fire strikes with heavy, bone-rattling low kicks to completely destroy her vertical base.

Raynare stumbled backward, her wings flapping erratically as she desperately tried to create distance.

Fajar pursued her relentlessly, shifting his stance. He drew both fists back to his waist, circulating every drop of his mortal internal energy, and unleashed the *Double Fist of the Black Turtle: First Stance - Basaltic Fist*. The explosive double-punch slammed squarely into Raynare's chest, the embedded shockwave of his will rippling through her internal organs.

She was launched backward, gasping for air, but Fajar was already moving. He followed up the explosive strike with a brutal, full-body shoulder tackle, completely blowing Raynare off her feet and sending her crashing violently into a stone pillar.

Watching her leaders get systematically dismantled by a single, terrifyingly aggressive high schooler, Mittelt completely lost her composure. "You monster! Die!" she screamed, abandoning all tactical sense and diving directly at Fajar from above, her parasol aimed at his neck.

Fajar didn't even look at her. His Future Sight had already mapped her desperate strike. Before she was even within striking distance, Fajar planted his left foot and executed the *Recoilless Three Stage Hoechook*.

In a span of time almost undetectable to the human eye, Fajar unleashed three distinct, rotational kicks—striking her jaw, her temple, and the back of her neck in a continuous, physics-defying blur of motion. The sheer concussive trauma left Mittelt suspended in the air, completely paralyzed.

Ren materialized from the shadow of the fountain, his dark cloak swirling. "Allow me to assist." The tactician followed up instantly, delivering a rapid sequence of shallow, agonizing slices across Mittelt’s exposed arms with his tactical knife, before pivoting into a flawless roundhouse kick that blew the blonde Fallen Angel away, sending her rolling across the dirt to land in a heap next to Raynare.

A few feet away, Kalawarner was breathing heavily, clutching her bruised sides as Ariel continued to dance around her with a terrifyingly bright smile. "What's wrong? I thought angels had better stamina!" Ariel taunted.

Kalawarner gritted her teeth in absolute despair. *This is impossible! They have no magic! They are just humans! But their technique... it's like fighting gods!*

Realizing they were seconds away from total annihilation, Kalawarner leaped backward, frantically drawing a glowing, teleportation magic circle in the air with her bloodied fingers. "Dohnaseek! Raynare! Mittelt! Fall back immediately!"

The battered Fallen Angels dragged themselves toward the expanding magic circle, their eyes filled with humiliation and rage.

"We are not leaving empty-handed!" Dohnaseek roared, wiping blood from his chin. "Eradicate the witnesses!"

In a final, spiteful act of desperation, all four Fallen Angels summoned every ounce of their remaining magical reserves. The sky above the park illuminated with a blinding, terrifying golden light as dozens of massive light spears materialized, humming with lethal, explosive heat.

With a unified shriek of fury, they hurled the entire barrage not at Fajar, Ariel, or Ren—but directly at Issei, who was trembling in the grass, and Matsuda and Motohama, who were cowering in the bushes.

"We're dead!" Matsuda howled, throwing his arms over his head.

"The probability of survival is zero!" Motohama sobbed, clutching the dirt.

Issei could only stare up at the descending apocalypse, his vision going entirely white.

Fajar remained perfectly calm. He didn't rush toward the civilians. Instead, he simply reached out a hand toward the tactician standing beside him.

"Ren," Fajar said smoothly, his eyes locked onto the descending barrage of divine light. "Let me borrow your extendable pole."

His breathing was wet and shallow, his blood rapidly pooling across the cracked pavement as the life began to fade from his eyes.

**Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 6**

The oppressive silence that settled over the destroyed park plaza was broken only by the shallow, wet gasping of Issei Hyoudou. He lay completely motionless in the center of the scorched crater, his school uniform soaked through with his own rapidly pooling blood. The massive, jagged wound in his abdomen—a direct byproduct of the concentrated divine bombardment—was catastrophic. For a normal human, it was a definitively fatal injury, the kind that promised total organ failure within a matter of minutes.

Fajar walked casually across the cracked concrete, his hands slipping back into his pockets as the terrifying, predatory aura that had completely broken the Fallen Angels vanished as quickly as it had appeared. He stopped at the edge of the crater and looked down at the dying boy. Kneeling beside Issei, Fajar placed his bare hands directly over the searing wound. He did not use magic, nor did he tap into any god-tier multiversal power. Instead, Fajar flawlessly circulated his minimum, baseline human internal energy, threading it into Issei’s failing biological systems just enough to slow the catastrophic bleeding and artificially sustain his fading heartbeat.

"Hyoudou Issei," Fajar said, his voice entirely devoid of panic or urgency, carrying the casual curiosity of someone asking about the weather. "How does dying feel like?"

Before Issei could even process the absurdity of the question, a blur of motion arrived at Fajar's side. Ariel dropped to his knees in the dirt, his face tight with uncharacteristic seriousness. He immediately placed his own hands next to Fajar's, seamlessly syncing his internal energy circulation with his leader's to act as a localized, biological painkiller.

"Bro, seriously?" Ariel hissed, shooting Fajar a deeply disapproving glare. "The kid is literally minutes away from bleeding out, and you're treating it like a psychological interview! How can you ask something so unbelievably insensitive at a time like this?"

"Because it is an entirely valid empirical question, and one he is uniquely positioned to answer," Ren said as he smoothly descended into the crater beside them.

The tactician knelt, placing his hands near Issei’s collarbone to help regulate the dying boy's internal temperature and stabilize the shock wracking his nervous system. Ren kept his eyes locked on the fading light in Issei's pupils, his expression a mask of melancholic nostalgia.

"This scene is highly reminiscent of our past, is it not?" Ren murmured quietly, the ambient noise of the bubbling park fountain framing his words. "Back in the fiction-to-reality community. You were always the unstoppable vanguard, Fajar. You charged the absolute front lines, tearing through the enemy ranks with unparalleled efficiency. But the collateral damage was always absolute. Everyone stationed behind you... every single comrade trying to hold the rear... they all died."

Fajar did not break his concentration on Issei's life-force, but a faint, chillingly calm smirk touched his lips. "That is a slight mischaracterization of the historical record, Ren. I was not simply charging the front lines; I was engaged in localized combat with entities of absolute, overwhelming strength. I applied such concentrated, lethal pressure that continuing to fight me became a mathematical net loss for them. I forced their strongest combatants to initiate a full-scale tactical retreat because engaging with me was entirely unprofitable."

Fajar's smile slowly faded, leaving behind a cold, hollow gaze that seemed to pierce through the very fabric of the universe. "But yes. You are correct about the aftermath. When they retreated and I finally walked back to the rear guard... there were only bodies waiting for me."

The sheer gravity of the conversation—a casual reflection on a multiversal massacre—hung over the dying boy. Fajar looked back down, his eyes refocusing on the present.

"I will ask you again, Hyoudou Issei," Fajar prompted softly. "How does dying feel like?"

Issei was completely beyond the point of questioning his reality. The agony in his gut had faded into a numbing, icy hollow. He did not care who these strange boys were, how they had fought off winged demons, or what incomprehensible wars they were talking about. His consciousness was unraveling, drifting lazily toward a pure, blinding white light.

"It... it hurts," Issei gasped, his voice barely a wet whisper. He slowly, agonizingly raised his trembling hand, staring blankly at the thick, crimson blood coating his fingers. "It hurts so much... but..."

Issei’s eyes glazed over, losing their focus on the night sky. "This red... it's not beautiful at all. It's not... as crimson red as her hair."

Ariel and Ren exchanged a quick, knowing glance, maintaining their energy circulation to give the boy just enough breath to finish.

"The first time I saw her..." Issei smiled weakly, a solitary tear sliding down his dirt-streaked cheek. "I was... completely captivated. If I really have to die here... it would be nice... if I could die on her breast. While being hugged by her..."

Fajar chuckled, a genuine sound of amusement echoing in the quiet park. His eyes flashed with the terrifying clarity of Advanced Observation Haki, peering just a few seconds into the immediate future. "Your romantic perseverance is genuinely commendable, Hyoudou. And as it turns out, my foresight indicates that the blood rapidly soaking through your trousers is currently activating the crumpled paper magic circle you shoved into your pocket this afternoon. I believe your final wish is about to be granted."

The exact moment Fajar finished speaking, a blinding, localized pulse of crimson demonic energy erupted from Issei's pocket. Fajar, Ariel, and Ren simultaneously withdrew their hands, effortlessly leaping backward out of the crater in synchronized precision to give the magic room to breathe.

The crimson light expanded, etching a massive, intricate Gremory crest directly into the scorched pavement. The air pressure in the park shifted violently, completely overwriting the lingering divine residue of the Fallen Angels with a heavy, suffocating aura of pure, high-class demonic power.

From the center of the glowing circle, Rias Gremory materialized.

The crimson-haired heiress stepped onto the battlefield with an expression of absolute, regal authority, fully expecting to find a dying boy bleeding out alone, perhaps with a low-level Fallen Angel lingering nearby waiting for execution. Instead, she stepped out of the portal and immediately froze.

Her demonic senses aggressively scanned the environment, but the data she received made absolutely no sense. Issei was indeed dying in a crater, but standing perfectly casually around him were three Kuoh Academy students. They possessed zero demonic energy, zero angelic light, and zero magical fluctuations. They were entirely, utterly baseline humans. Yet, their uniforms were completely unbattered, and they radiated an incomprehensible, terrifying calm in the center of a supernaturally devastated war zone.

Fajar dusted his hands off, offering Rias a polite, perfectly deadpan smile. "He specifically requested crimson hair and a soft chest to die on. The floor is yours, President."

Rias’s cerulean eyes narrowed, her mind racing. She had no idea what had transpired here. Her familiar, Koneko, was supposed to be observing from afar and had not yet delivered a reconnaissance report. Rias was completely blind to the tactical reality of the situation, but one fact remained absolute: the host of the Boosted Gear was mere seconds away from total biological death.

Interrogating these impossible humans would have to wait.

Ignoring Fajar's brazen commentary, Rias rushed to Issei's side. "You've done well to survive this long, Issei," she whispered softly, her regal composure melting into deep, maternal empathy.

Understanding that a mortal body required absolute biological intimacy to properly merge with high-tier Evil Pieces, Rias did not hesitate. In a fluid, entirely unabashed motion, she unbuttoned her Kuoh Academy blouse, shedding her clothing to reveal her bare, flawless skin. The crimson magic of the summoning circle flared vibrantly as she gently lifted Issei from the blood-soaked dirt, pressing his head directly against her bare, soft breasts. She wrapped her arms around him in a deeply intimate, naked embrace, sharing her demonic body heat and transferring her life-force directly into his failing system.

"Live for me, Issei," Rias commanded softly, pulling the eight glowing Pawn pieces from her demonic space and pressing them into his chest, watching as they sank seamlessly into his heart to rebuild his flesh.

While the majestic, highly intimate resurrection ritual took place, the true casualty of the evening was occurring fifty meters away.

Hidden entirely within the dense, leafy perimeter of the park's bushes, Matsuda and Motohama were witnessing the absolute apex of supernatural beauty combined with their ultimate, unattainable erotic fantasy. They had just survived an apocalyptic orbital bombardment of holy light, narrowly escaping death by the grace of a multiversal vanguard, but all of that trauma was instantly, violently overwritten.

Matsuda was literally biting through the sleeve of his trench coat, tears of blood streaming down his face as he watched the school's most unapproachable, beautiful idol cradle his dying best friend naked. "He... he gets a beautiful demon princess... and we get to hide in the dirt! The universe is a cruel, mocking void!"

Motohama was aggressively clawing at the soil, his glasses completely fogged over with the sheer heat of his jealousy. "The statistical probability of this outcome is a negative integer! He has transcended humanity through the sheer power of perversion! I am dying! My soul is actually leaving my body!"

Back in the crater, the crimson glow slowly began to fade. The fatal wound on Issei's abdomen knitted completely shut, leaving behind unblemished skin. His breathing stabilized into a deep, rhythmic slumber.

Rias carefully wrapped herself in a conjured, thick crimson blanket, holding the unconscious, reincarnated Devil in her arms. She stood up, the Gremory magic circle already reforming beneath her bare feet to initiate a spatial teleportation back to Issei's bedroom.

She did not reach out to wipe the memories of the three boys standing before her. Erasing the minds of mortals was standard protocol, but Fajar, Ariel, and Ren were a catastrophic anomaly. Rias knew that attempting a memory wipe on entities she fundamentally did not understand could trigger a lethal defensive response. She needed Koneko's recon report. She needed to understand exactly what kind of monsters were hiding in plain sight within her territory before she made a single move.

Without uttering a single word of gratitude or inquiry, Rias cast one final, piercingly cold, intensely calculating glare at Fajar, Ariel, and Ren. The crimson light flared, and in the blink of an eye, the Gremory heiress and her new Pawn vanished from the park, leaving the multiversal veterans standing quietly in the devastated ruins of the plaza.

The atmosphere inside the Occult Research Clubroom was stiflingly heavy. The antique grandfather clock ticked rhythmically against the wall, but the sound felt muted beneath the suffocating tension. Rias Gremory sat behind her grand mahogany desk, her fingers steepled together, her cerulean eyes locked onto the petite, silver-haired girl standing in the center of the Persian rug.

Akeno Himejima stood perfectly still beside the window, her usual teasing, elegant smile completely absent. Yuuto Kiba leaned against the leather sofa, his arms crossed, his knightly composure fractured by a rare expression of deep, unsettling confusion.

Rias had just returned from Issei Hyoudou’s bedroom, having successfully completed the reincarnation ritual. But the image of those three unbothered, mundane teenagers standing in the center of a supernaturally devastated crater refused to leave her mind.

"Begin the report, Koneko," Rias ordered, her voice carefully controlled, masking the deep well of anxiety churning in her stomach. "Tell me exactly what transpired in that park before I arrived. Leave no detail out."

Koneko Toujou, the stoic Rook of the Gremory peerage, took a slow breath. Her golden eyes, usually entirely devoid of emotion, carried a faint, lingering tremor of genuine shock.

"The initial phase of the target's date proceeded as expected," Koneko began, her voice quiet but echoing clearly in the vast room. "However, the perimeter was compromised from the beginning. Issei Hyoudou was being aggressively surveilled by two mundane students—Matsuda and Motohama. Accompanying them were two other students. Ariel Veritas and Ren Veritas."

Kiba frowned, his brow furrowing. "The Veritas brothers? I know them. They transferred to Kuoh Academy a while ago. They are incredibly athletic, highly popular, but they actively choose to associate with Issei’s perverted trio. My sensory scans on them have never returned anything beyond a standard, baseline human signature."

"Your scans were functionally correct, but practically useless, Kiba-senpai," Koneko stated bluntly. "When the Fallen Angel Raynare dropped her disguise and initiated her execution strike on Issei, Ariel and Ren Veritas intervened. They did not use magic. They did not use Sacred Gears. They used pure, unadulterated physical kinetics."

Rias leaned forward, the leather of her chair creaking. "Explain."

"Ariel Veritas intercepted a materialized spear of light by physically tackling the Fallen Angel," Koneko said, delivering the impossible statement with clinical detachment. "His acceleration went from zero to maximum velocity in a fraction of a second. The biomechanical torque he generated lifted Raynare entirely off the ground and shattered her focus. Ren Veritas then engaged her in close-quarters combat using a standard, carbon-steel tactical knife."

"A mundane knife?" Kiba interjected, his pride as a magical swordsman genuinely offended. "That's impossible, Koneko. A weapon forged of pure, divine light would instantly melt through standard carbon steel upon contact, let alone the sheer kinetic force of a Fallen Angel's swing."

"He didn't block the light, senpai," Koneko replied, looking directly at the Knight. "He deflected the kinetic trajectory. He read the micro-contractions in her shoulder muscles, calculated the angle of her strike, and parried the divine weapon using irrefutable physics, striking the side of her blade where the magical density was weakest. He then systematically severed her tendons with surgical precision. To my eyes... it looked like they were fighting a slow, clumsy child. Raynare could not land a single strike on either of them."

Akeno inhaled sharply, bringing a hand to her cheek. "My, my... baseline humans completely dismantling a high-tier Fallen Angel? That completely rewrites our understanding of mortal limitations. But Rias found the park completely destroyed, and Issei was fatally wounded. If they were so dominant, how did the situation deteriorate?"

"Reinforcements," Koneko answered, her expression darkening. "Three more Fallen Angels descended. Kalawarner, Mittelt, and Dohnaseek. Even then, Ariel and Ren possessed the speed and technique to evade and counter. The battlefield dynamic only shifted because the Fallen Angels realized they could not hit the brothers, and instead targeted the absolute dead weight on the field: Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama."

Koneko paused, her small hands clenching into fists at her sides. "Ariel and Ren were artificially shackled. They willingly threw themselves into the crossfire, absorbing graze damage and explosive shockwaves to physically shield the mundane humans. It was a chaotic escort mission. But then... the unregistered variable entered the perimeter."

Rias’s eyes narrowed to dangerous slits. "The third boy. The one who spoke to me. I ran a mental cross-reference of the entire Kuoh Academy registry the moment I saw him. He was wearing our uniform, but he is not enrolled at our school. Who is he, Koneko?"

"I do not know his name, President. I have never seen him before in my life," Koneko admitted, a slight shiver running down her spine—a biological reaction she could not suppress. "But his presence... President, I have senjutsu. I can read the natural flow of life energy. When that boy stepped into the clearing, the ambient air pressure physically dropped. He possessed absolutely no magical aura, but his sheer, psychological presence was that of an apex predator. The Fallen Angels were subconsciously terrified before he even moved. Their magical defenses involuntarily wavered in his presence."

Kiba stepped forward, entirely captivated. "How did he fight?"

"With absolute, unmitigated violence," Koneko whispered. "He did not fight defensively like Ariel or Ren. He charged the frontline directly. Dohnaseek thrust a spear of light at him, and the boy didn't even attempt to block. He moved as if he already knew exactly where the spear would be seconds before it was thrown. He slipped past it, struck Dohnaseek’s solar plexus with a rotational knee strike that bypassed his supernatural durability entirely, and then threw him into the concrete hard enough to crater the plaza."

Akeno’s smile was completely gone. "A human... physically throwing Dohnaseek?"

"He then engaged Raynare," Koneko continued, her voice gaining a rapid, almost breathless cadence. "A flawless barrage of close-quarters chain punches, followed by a double-fist strike that sent a shockwave through her internal organs. Mittelt attempted to ambush him from above. He didn't even look at her. He executed a three-stage rotational kick in mid-air that paralyzed her nervous system. When the Fallen Angels attempted a final, desperate orbital bombardment of light spears to cover their retreat, he borrowed Ren's extendable pole, walked directly into the falling artillery, and physically beat the remaining magic out of them until they teleported away weeping."

Silence reigned in the clubroom for a long, suffocating minute. Rias stared at her desk, her mind working furiously to categorize this apocalyptic data.

"They let Issei take the fatal hit," Rias concluded softly, a cold, aristocratic anger bleeding into her tone. "If they possessed the speed and foresight you describe, they could have saved all three of the boys. Did they deliberately use Issei as a sacrificial pawn? Did they know about our monitoring? Are they agents of the Church attempting to manipulate the Gremory clan into a proxy war?"

"No, President," Koneko answered immediately, her tone absolute and unwavering.

Rias looked up, surprised by her Rook's immediate dismissal. "You sound certain, Koneko."

"I am," Koneko nodded, stepping closer to the desk. "I observed their micro-expressions, monitored their heart rates, and read their lips throughout the entire engagement. There is no grand conspiracy, President. They possess absolutely zero manipulative intent toward the Occult Research Club. In fact... they barely care that we exist."

Kiba blinked, taken aback. "They don't care? But they let Issei die."

"They knew Issei possessed the Gremory summoning flyer," Koneko explained meticulously. "They knew that if Issei suffered a fatal injury, the paper would activate and you would arrive to resurrect him as a Devil. They calculated that Issei already had a supernatural safety net backing him. Matsuda and Motohama did not."

Koneko looked directly into Rias’s eyes. "When the orbital bombardment began, they made a cold, instantaneous tactical calculation. They could not protect all three civilians perfectly. So, they abandoned the one who had an immortal medical evacuation waiting for him, and threw their entire defensive output into shielding Matsuda and Motohama—their mundane friends who had absolutely no one else to save them. They didn't do it to manipulate you, President. They did it because they genuinely wanted to save their friends, and..."

Koneko hesitated, swallowing hard. "...and because they were having fun."

"Fun?" Akeno repeated, her voice barely a whisper.

"Yes," Koneko confirmed, her golden eyes wide. "They were smiling. They were bantering. Ariel and Ren were treating high-class Fallen Angels like sparring partners. And that unknown boy... he was treating them like literal punching bags. To them, this wasn't a desperate battle for survival. It was recreation."

Rias Gremory slowly leaned back in her chair, the sheer weight of the revelation settling over her shoulders like a lead mantle. Her territory, the town she ruled as the Crimson-Haired Ruin Princess, was currently housing three entities masquerading as human teenagers. Entities who possessed no magic, yet could effortlessly dismantle divine beings with pure martial arts and overwhelming willpower. Entities who viewed Devil reincarnation not as a miraculous, life-altering pact, but as a convenient ambulance service they could reliably pawn their injured friend off on while they enjoyed a supernatural brawl.

"Keep observing them, Koneko," Rias commanded quietly, her voice trembling with a mixture of profound dread and intense, overwhelming curiosity. "Do not engage. Do not provoke them. We need to figure out exactly what it is that has decided to make Kuoh Academy its playground."

He glanced over at the two unconscious teenagers snoring softly in the bushes. "I will open a dimensional corridor through the Harrowing Interstice. We can teleport them directly into their respective beds to avoid any further logistical complications."

"Hold on, bro! Cancel the portal," Ariel grinned, walking over and effortlessly hoisting Matsuda over his left shoulder and Motohama over his right like two sacks of flour. "I haven't had a proper workout all week because of the limiters. Carrying two dead-weight teenagers across town is decent dynamic resistance training. We walk."

Ren sighed softly, adjusting his dark cloak. "Very well. A pedestrian escort it is."

The three multiversal anomalies strolled out of the ruined park, leaving the magical anomalies and destroyed concrete behind them. They navigated the quiet, dimly lit streets of Kuoh Town, the cool autumn wind carrying the casual, joyful tone of their conversation.

"Fajar," Ren spoke up, his analytical mind still processing the battlefield data. "Your vanguard charge tonight was entirely reckless by conventional tactical standards, yet your execution was flawless. You did not just read their intentions; you preempted their physical mechanics before the kinetic signals even fired. How did you achieve that level of precision without utilizing your higher-dimensional speed?"

Fajar walked with his hands stuffed in his pockets, gazing up at the streetlights. "It's an application of advanced sensory perception. I wasn't just sensing the surrounding environment or reading their killing intent. I was quite literally foreseeing the future."

Ariel’s eyes lit up with intense, unrestrained anime-fanboy enthusiasm. He nearly dropped Motohama in his excitement. "Wait, seriously?! Like Katakuri’s Advanced Observation Haki from *One Piece*? You were looking seconds into the future?!"

"Exactly like that," Fajar affirmed with a warm smile. "When you push your willpower and sensory mastery to the absolute pinnacle, the linear flow of time becomes a readable variable. I saw their attacks, the trajectory, and the resulting damage before they even summoned their weapons."

Ren’s dark eyes narrowed with quiet, burning determination. "Future Sight... I see. That is the next logical evolution of my sensory capabilities. I am adding that to my training regimen immediately. I will begin tomorrow morning."

Ariel shifted Matsuda's weight on his shoulder, his grin widening. "I knew it! And those strikes you used on Raynare and Dohnaseek—those were strictly from *The God of High School*, right? I recognized the Renewal Recoilless Baekdu and the Basaltic Fist anywhere!"

"Good eye," Fajar laughed. "Yes, they were. There is a profound beauty in mortal martial arts. Remember back in the *God of High School* narrative? Even the Jade Emperor, Okhwang—the absolute pinnacle of divine authority—eventually started learning human martial arts because he recognized their terrifying, undeniable effectiveness against raw magical power."

"Exactly!" Ariel cheered. "Gods rely too much on their destructive yields! They completely forget about biomechanical torque!"

Their joyful, animated banter carried them through the suburban streets. They made a quick detour to Matsuda's house, where Ariel casually hopped a two-story fence to drop the boy through his open bedroom window, before doing the exact same for Motohama a few blocks later. With the civilians safely secured, they finally made their way back to the Veritas household.

They stood on the front porch under the warm, amber glow of the porch light. Fajar stretched his arms over his head, a relaxed sigh escaping his lips.

"Well, my designated maintenance job here is done," Fajar said, his form subtly beginning to shimmer at the edges as the spatial reality around him began to warp. "I am returning to the Infinite Reality realm."

Ariel frowned, visibly disappointed. "Aw, come on! Why not just stick around? Now that the limiters are off, we can actually enjoy the Kuoh Academy slice-of-life properly. You should stay!"

"I concur," Ren added smoothly. "Your presence would provide an excellent sparring baseline for my Future Sight training."

Fajar smiled, the shimmering distortion around his body growing brighter. "That is genuinely a great idea, and I would love to. But I manifested here too suddenly to perform the limiter removal. To stay long-term in this specific narrative layer without collapsing the local dimensional physics, I need the proper time to forge a stable Avatar and embed a true fragment of my soul into it. If I stay in this temporary projection, I'll accidentally break the planet."

Fajar offered a lazy, two-finger salute as his physical form began to dissolve into pure, ambient starlight. "I'll do the paperwork and build a proper vessel. See you both next time."

With a silent, non-kinetic flash, the Heavenly Demon vanished from the porch, leaving Ariel and Ren standing alone in the quiet night, fully unrestrained and ready to truly begin their lives in Kuoh.

### Route 4 Life 0 Section 3 Sub Section 9

Issei Hyoudou bolted upright in his bed, a strangled gasp tearing from his throat. His hands flew instinctively to his stomach, fully expecting to feel the slick, terrifying warmth of his own blood and the gaping, jagged hole left by the Fallen Angel's orbital bombardment. Instead, his fingers met smooth, unblemished skin and the soft fabric of his pajama shirt. He scrambled out of bed, nearly tripping over a stack of discarded adult magazines, and practically threw himself at the full-length mirror.

Nothing. There was not a single scratch, scar, or bruise on his torso.

"Was it... a dream?" Issei muttered, his heart hammering against his ribs like a trapped bird. But the phantom sensation of searing, localized heat and the lingering scent of ozone and copper felt entirely too real. And worse, his last memory was the terrifyingly calm face of a strange boy, the sudden, intoxicating smell of high-class perfume, and the sensation of bare, impossibly soft breasts pressing against his face.

Unable to contain the suffocating anxiety, Issei haphazardly threw on his weekend clothes and sprinted out of his house, his feet carrying him directly toward the park. When he arrived, the sheer, undeniable reality of the situation punched all the air from his lungs. The plaza was a devastated war zone. Deep, scorched craters littered the concrete, the fountain was violently shattered, and the benches were reduced to splintered kindling.

"It wasn't a dream," Issei whispered, his eyes widening in absolute horror as the memories flooded back with agonizing clarity. The light spears. The strange, overwhelmingly powerful transfer students. The absolute massacre. "Matsuda! Motohama!"

Driven by sheer, panicked adrenaline, Issei sprinted toward the residential district. He didn't have to search long. Sitting on a low brick wall outside a local convenience store, looking like two war veterans who had just survived a multi-year deployment, were Matsuda and Motohama. They were both aggressively slurping down boxes of strawberry milk, their eyes ringed with heavy, dark bags.

"Guys!" Issei yelled, skidding to a halt in front of them. "You're alive! You're completely fine!"

Matsuda slowly lowered his milk carton, his gaze entirely hollow. "Hyoudou... I want to punch you in the jaw so badly right now, but my arms feel like wet noodles. Do you have any idea what we went through last night?"

Motohama violently adjusted his glasses, his hands trembling. "The statistical probability of three individuals experiencing the exact same highly detailed, traumatic, and erotic hallucination is functionally zero. Ergo, reality itself has fractured, or we survived an actual encounter with winged demons who got beaten half to death by Kuoh Academy transfer students."

"So it was real," Issei groaned, gripping his hair. "The light spears... the craters..."

"Oh, it was real," Matsuda suddenly sobbed, fat tears rolling down his cheeks. "It was all real! We almost got vaporized by holy orbital strikes, but that's not even the worst part! The worst part was watching you, you absolute degenerate, get coddled and resurrected by President Rias Gremory! Naked! She hugged you naked! Why does the universe reward your idiocy with the ultimate high school fantasy while we get shoved into the dirt?!"

"Wait, naked?!" Issei yelled, a massive blush erupting across his face as the hazy, dreamlike memory suddenly snapped into high-definition focus. "That actually happened?! I thought that was just my brain shutting down!"

"I am mathematically calculating the exact angle I need to throw myself into traffic to reincarnate into a protagonist," Motohama muttered darkly, staring at the asphalt. "Let's just agree it was a gas leak. A highly localized, hallucinogenic gas leak that specifically targeted our perversions."

"I don't think it's a gas leak," Issei said softly, blinking in extreme confusion as he looked around the street. "Guys... something is wrong with me. I can... hear things."

Issei focused his gaze on a stray cat sitting on a fence three blocks away, realizing with mounting terror that he could perfectly hear its heartbeat, the soft rustle of its fur, and the tiny scratching of its claws against the wood. When he looked at Motohama, his vision auto-focused to the point where he could count the individual microscopic scratches on the lenses of his glasses. The sensory overload was dizzying. He was no longer human, but his mortal brain hadn't caught up to his demonic physiology yet.

Desperate to normalize the situation, the trio decided to seek refuge in absolute, mundane banality. They bought cheap snacks and aimlessly wandered down a quiet, abandoned commercial alleyway behind the arcade, desperately trying to distract themselves with arguments over their favorite gravure idols.

But the supernatural world was not done with them.

The ambient temperature in the alley plummeted. The sky above them seemed to artificially darken, the shadows lengthening ominously against the brick walls. A heavy, suffocating pressure washed over the alleyway.

"Look up," a deep, arrogant voice commanded from the sky.

The three boys froze, slowly raising their heads. Hovering twenty feet above them, his black feathered wings fully extended, was Dohnaseek. The Fallen Angel looked significantly worse for wear compared to the previous night, sporting dark bruises and a thoroughly humiliated disposition, but his magical aura was flaring with lethal intent. Utilizing his supernatural senses, he had tracked them down. Because the multiversal limiters on Ariel and Ren had been removed, Dohnaseek's radar only picked up the three weak, baseline signatures of the perverted trio. He assumed they were alone and completely defenseless.

"You humiliating little rats," Dohnaseek sneered, manifesting a crackling, superheated spear of pure light in his right hand. "Did you really think you could survive an encounter with the Fallen, witness our humiliation, and simply walk away? I will incinerate you until not even your ashes remain!"

A few blocks away, standing atop a water tower, the Occult Research Club was watching the confrontation unfold. Rias narrowed her eyes, observing Issei’s demonic aura instinctively flaring up in response to the threat.

"President, should we intervene?" Kiba asked, his hand resting on the hilt of his unseen sword.

"Hold your position," Rias commanded calmly. "Issei is a Devil now. The innate physical durability of the Gremory Pawn piece is more than enough to tank a standard light spear. Let him take the hit. It will force his demonic powers to fully awaken and solidify his understanding of his new reality."

Dohnaseek roared, throwing his arm forward. The spear of light shot down toward Issei like a localized lightning bolt, illuminating the dark alleyway with blinding, lethal radiance. Issei threw his arms up in a pathetic, entirely human attempt to shield himself, squeezing his eyes shut as Matsuda and Motohama screamed in terror.

But the explosion never came.

Instead, a sharp, concussive boom echoed through the alley, followed by the sound of shattering glass.

Issei slowly opened his eyes. Standing directly in front of him, having closed the distance so fast he simply appeared as a localized blur of displaced air, was Ariel Veritas. The athletic transfer student wasn't standing in a tactical guard, nor was he employing any complex martial arts. He was simply holding his right hand out.

Clutched tightly in Ariel's bare, unprotected palm was the tip of the superheated light spear.

Dohnaseek's jaw dropped, his eyes bulging in absolute, uncomprehending horror. A baseline human attempting to touch a weapon forged of pure holy light should have resulted in instantaneous, agonizing vaporization.

"Man, you guys just don't know when to quit, do you?" Ariel sighed, an energetic, almost bored smile on his face.

With a casual, terrifying flex of his uncapped physical strength, Ariel closed his fist. The indestructible, divine light spear shattered into a million harmless, glittering sparks that drifted down around him like snow.

Before Dohnaseek could even process the impossible display of physical dominance, the shadows cast by the alley's dumpsters violently warped and elongated. The darkness surged upward, bypassing the physical distance entirely, and instantly coalesced into four massive, jagged, obsidian spikes that erupted directly from Dohnaseek's own shadow.

*Schhhk!*

The Fallen Angel shrieked in agony as the solid shadow spikes impaled him through the shoulders, wings, and lower back, completely immobilizing him in mid-air. He writhed helplessly, bleeding out magical energy as he looked frantically around for the source of the attack.

Leaning casually against the brick wall near the alley's entrance, bathed in the dim light of his smartphone screen, was Ren Veritas. He wasn't even looking at the Fallen Angel. His thumbs were rapidly tapping the screen as he navigated a high-level digital chess match.

"Knight to E4. Check," Ren murmured quietly to himself, before finally lifting his dark, apathetic eyes to the bleeding entity suspended in the sky. "Allow me to clarify the current paradigm, Fallen Angel. Last night, Ariel and I were severely dimensionally limited, forced to rely exclusively on baseline human kinetics and biomechanical redirection to fight you. We did this purely as a localized handicap for our own entertainment."

Ren pocketed his phone, the air around him suddenly distorting as a terrifying, boundless, uncapped aura of multiversal pressure bled into the alleyway. The sheer weight of it made the brick walls groan and crack.

"Those limiters are no longer active," Ren continued, his voice cold and devoid of all mercy. "If you ever attempt to threaten the lives of our friends again, we will not merely humiliate you with martial arts. We will systematically dismantle your atomic structure until you cease to exist across all observable realities."

"W-What are you?!" Dohnaseek gasped, coughing up blood. "You're not human! You're monsters!"

Before Ren could finalize the execution, a blinding, majestic crimson magic circle erupted on the ground beneath them. The heavy, suffocating aura of high-class demonic power instantly flooded the alleyway, aggressively clashing with the lingering divine light and Ren’s multiversal pressure.

Rias Gremory rose from the teleportation circle, flanked flawlessly by Akeno, Kiba, and Koneko. Her crimson hair flared violently, her cerulean eyes locked onto the suspended Fallen Angel with the absolute, uncompromising authority of a monarch defending her borders.

"That is quite enough," Rias declared, her voice echoing with commanding, regal power. "You have trespassed deep into Kuoh Town, Fallen Angel. This entire territory is under the exclusive, sovereign jurisdiction of the Gremory clan. Any further aggressive action against my servants or the citizens of this town will be interpreted as a direct act of war against the Underworld."

Dohnaseek stared at the crimson-haired heiress, the pieces finally snapping into place. He looked from Rias to the terrified, trembling Issei, feeling the distinct, undeniable demonic signature now radiating from the boy he thought he had killed.

"A reincarnated Devil..." Dohnaseek choked out, his arrogance entirely shattered. He realized he was not only hopelessly outmatched by the two anomalous monsters pinning him to the sky, but he was also staring down a high-class Devil peerage. "I am Dohnaseek. Grigori operative. We... we have no intention of inciting an all-out factional war over this territory. This was a localized assassination directive that has clearly been compromised. We will retreat."

Ren quickly processed the political variables of the situation. Continuing the execution in front of the local supernatural authority would unnecessarily complicate their slice-of-life retirement plan. With a completely dismissive sigh, the tactician pulled his phone back out and resumed his chess game.

"Acceptable," Ren said quietly. He snapped his fingers without looking up.

The obsidian shadow spikes instantly dissolved into black mist. Dohnaseek plummeted out of the sky, barely catching himself with his battered wings just before he hit the asphalt. Panting heavily, clutching his bleeding wounds, the Fallen Angel manifested a crude teleportation circle beneath him, casting one last terrified look at Ariel and Ren before vanishing into a flash of golden light.

Silence descended upon the alleyway, broken only by the soft *beep* of Ren’s chess app declaring a checkmate.

Rias turned her gaze away from the empty space where Dohnaseek had been, her expression shifting from regal authority to a carefully guarded, intensely calculating calm. She looked at Issei, who was currently hyperventilating against a dumpster, and then at Matsuda and Motohama, who had seamlessly fainted into a tangled heap on the concrete for the second time in twenty-four hours. Finally, her eyes settled on Ariel and Ren, who were radiating an aura of completely casual indifference.

"This situation has escalated beyond casual oversight," Rias said, her tone leaving absolutely no room for argument. "It is clear that the reality of this town has shifted dramatically, and you all have been thrust into the center of it. Take your friends home. Rest and recover your strength."

Rias turned her back, her crimson hair flowing behind her as the teleportation circle began to glow once more.

"We will convene at the Occult Research Club room tomorrow after school," Rias finalized, casting a sidelong glance at Issei. "All of you. We have an extensive amount of history to discuss."

### Life 1 Section 1 Sub Section 1

The morning commute to Kuoh Academy was usually filled with the loud, highly inappropriate, and aggressively animated chatter of the school's most notorious trio. However, on this crisp Monday morning, Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama walked in a state of stunned, uncomprehending silence. Their eyes were glued to the figure walking perfectly in stride beside them.

Ren Veritas was wearing a thick, impenetrable band of black fabric wrapped tightly over his eyes, completely obscuring his vision.

"Okay, I'll bite," Matsuda finally said, breaking the awkward silence as he pointed a trembling finger at the blindfold. "What exactly is the narrative here, Ren? Are we doing a cosplay thing? Did you lose a bet? Or did you finally look at something so magnificently perverted that you decided to retire your eyes while you were at your peak?"

Ren didn't miss a single step, easily navigating the uneven pavement and a stray bicycle parked on the sidewalk with terrifying, fluid grace. "It is routine sensory deprivation training," Ren answered, his voice smooth and entirely devoid of irony. "My current baseline capabilities are insufficient. I am attempting to force my auxiliary senses to evolve so that I can bridge the insurmountable gap between my current self and Fajar."

The mere mention of that name caused a collective, involuntary shudder to ripple through the perverted trio. The memory of the park incident—the apocalyptic craters, the descending light spears, and the terrifying, god-like aura of the boy named Fajar physically dismantling winged demons with a steel pole—was permanently burned into their retinas.

Under normal circumstances, the trio would have relentlessly interrogated Ren about his sudden, bizarre shift in behavior and the complete, unnatural evaporation of his perverted tendencies. But after surviving an orbital magic bombardment and witnessing the literal resurrection of their best friend, their threshold for absurdity had drastically expanded. If Ren said he was training to catch up to a multiversal apex predator, they were inclined to believe him.

"I... see," Motohama muttered, pushing his glasses up the bridge of his nose. "Given the recent paradigm shift in our observable reality, voluntarily blinding yourself for martial arts training is statistically one of the least crazy things I've witnessed this week."

Ren turned his head slightly toward them, his tone softening with genuine warmth despite his stoic expression. "I appreciate your understanding. And please, do not let my personal martial pursuits alienate you. Regardless of our differing trajectories, we are still friends forever."

"Heck yeah, we are!" Ariel chimed in from the rear, flashing a massive, sunny grin. He jogged up to join the front of the group, though every step he took was accompanied by the heavy, metallic clanking of dense iron. Ariel's Kuoh Academy uniform was noticeably bulging, stretched taut over a series of thick, cumbersome training weights strapped to his chest, arms, and calves.

"I'm actually planning to start the blindfold training later this evening," Ariel declared proudly, rolling his shoulders with a heavy grunt. "For now, I'm focusing on dynamic kinetic resistance! Though, honestly, I'm extremely disappointed in the local sporting goods stores. I bought literally every ankle and vest weight they had in stock, and it barely feels like a heavy winter coat."

Internally, Ariel sighed. *Mundane iron is useless. The density is all wrong. I need to contact Fajar later and ask him to forge me some localized gravitational anomaly weights from the Infinite Reality realm. Maybe something forged from a dying dwarf star.*

As the group finally approached the grand iron gates of Kuoh Academy, the bustling morning atmosphere washed over them. For a normal human, it was just the loud, chaotic hum of hundreds of teenagers. But for Ren, whose hyper-senses were dialed to the absolute maximum to compensate for his lack of sight, and for Ariel, whose Advanced Observation Haki passively blanketed the courtyard, the environment was a crystal-clear tapestry of biological rhythms, emotional spikes, and isolated conversations.

Specifically, they easily picked up the aggressive, localized whispering of the female student body.

*"Look at the Veritas brothers..."* a second-year girl murmured to her friend near the shoe lockers. *"Is Ren actually blindfolded?"*

*"I told you he changed!"* another girl hissed excitedly from the staircase. *"Remember last week when Issei and the others were trying to peek through the chain-link fence at the girls' tennis club? Ren didn't even look! He sat under a tree playing digital chess on his phone the entire time! And now he's literally wearing a blindfold! You can't be a pervert if you physically refuse to look at anything!"*

*"But why is he doing it?"* a third chimed in, a faint blush on her cheeks. *"It looks so extreme and ascetic... like a mysterious martial arts monk. It’s kind of incredibly hot."*

Ariel nudged his brother’s ribs with a heavy, weighted elbow, a wide, teasing grin on his face. "Way to go, brother. You accidentally engineered a massive PR campaign. The girls think you've shed the 'Beast of Perversion' title to become a mysterious, tragic bad boy. You're a heartthrob now."

Ren sighed, perfectly dodging a student who was running late without even shifting his posture. "I assure you, Ariel, social engineering was the furthest thing from my mind. I had completely forgotten about our deliberately cultivated perverted reputations. I am simply desperate. The memory of Fajar’s Future Sight is haunting me. I cannot rest until my sensory network reaches that exact multiversal frequency."

The school day passed in a blur of mundane classes, a stark and jarring contrast to the supernatural violence of the weekend. When the final bell of the afternoon finally rang, the students began packing their bags, chatting eagerly about club activities and weekend plans.

Suddenly, a collective, breathless sigh swept through the female population of the classroom. The atmosphere instantly shifted as Yuuto Kiba, the undisputed Prince of Kuoh Academy and Knight of the Gremory peerage, stepped through the sliding classroom door. He radiated an aura of flawless, knightly elegance, his polite smile immediately captivating every girl in the room.

However, the swooning quickly morphed into profound, collective confusion when Kiba bypassed the popular crowds entirely and walked directly toward the back corner of the room.

"Excuse me," Kiba said, his voice smooth and perfectly modulated. "Hyoudou Issei-kun. The President of the Occult Research Club would like to see you in the old school building."

The girls in the classroom physically recoiled. *Hyoudou? The biggest pervert in the school? Why on earth would the beautiful, untouchable Rias Gremory want anything to do with him?*

Kiba politely ignored the murmurs and turned his gaze toward the two transfers sitting nearby. "Ariel-kun. Ren-kun. The President extends her invitation to both of you as well. If you would please accompany us."

Instantly, the girls in the classroom nodded in synchronized, understanding approval. *That* made perfect sense. Ariel was an athletic giant with a sunny disposition, and Ren was the mysterious, blindfolded stoic. Of course the elite Occult Research Club would want to recruit the Veritas brothers. The fact that Issei was included was clearly just an unfortunate bureaucratic oversight.

Matsuda and Motohama, however, completely ignored Kiba's polite request to Ariel and Ren. Having witnessed the Veritas brothers literally punch Fallen Angels through concrete, the duo held a deep, terrified respect for them. They knew better than to question their involvement in occult matters.

Issei, on the other hand, was still their peer in the gutter of high school hierarchy.

"Hyoudou, you absolute traitor!" Matsuda roared comedically, tears of pure, unadulterated venom streaming down his face as he lunged forward, grabbing Issei by the collar. "What kind of dark, forbidden blood pact did you sign to get an escort from the Prince to see President Gremory?!"

"You are a biological anomaly that must be studied and subsequently destroyed!" Motohama shrieked, biting down on his handkerchief as he adjusted his glasses with a violently trembling hand. "You die in a park and suddenly you're entering the highest echelon of the school's social stratum! I curse you, Issei! I curse your entire bloodline!"

To be continued in next sub section.

### Life 1 Section 1 Sub Section 2

The atmosphere inside the Occult Research Clubroom was a study in contrasts. Sunlight filtered through the antique stained-glass windows, casting warm, colorful patterns across the Persian rug, yet the air was thick with an oppressive, undeniable tension.

Issei Hyoudou stood near the center of the room, looking entirely out of his depth. Behind Rias Gremory’s imposing mahogany desk, the Crimson-Haired Ruin Princess sat with her fingers steepled, her cerulean eyes locked onto the trio before her. Akeno Himejima stood by the window, her usual teasing smile replaced by a look of sharp calculation. Kiba Yuuto leaned against the wall, his posture relaxed but his hand resting inches from where he would summon his demonic sword. Koneko Toujou sat on a velvet sofa, quietly snacking on a chocolate bar, though her golden eyes never left Ariel and Ren.

"Hyoudou Issei," Rias began, her voice echoing with commanding authority. "Let us dispense with the pleasantries. The girl who asked you on a date, Amano Yuma, was a Fallen Angel named Raynare. Her sole objective was to assassinate you."

Issei physically recoiled, his face draining of color. "A Fallen Angel? Like... from the Bible? But why me?! I'm just a normal high school student!"

"Because you possess a Sacred Gear," Rias explained patiently, summoning a faint crimson aura to her fingertips to emphasize her point. "Artifacts of immense power bestowed upon humans by God. Yours is particularly dangerous, which drew the attention of the Fallen Angels. When Raynare dealt the fatal blow, the flyer you received from me activated. I arrived and used my demonic power to resurrect you."

Rias stood up, her crimson hair flowing behind her like a regal cape. "This world is divided in a hidden, eternal stalemate between three major factions: Angels, Fallen Angels, and Devils. As of last night, you are no longer human, Issei. I reincarnated you as a Devil. You are now my servant, a member of the Gremory peerage."

Issei stood frozen, his brain struggling to process the sheer weight of the supernatural lore being dumped onto his shoulders. Devils. Angels. Sacred Gears. He looked down at his hands, expecting to see claws, but they looked exactly the same. He looked back at Rias, taking in her flawless, breathtaking beauty, the absolute conviction in her eyes, and the memory of her warm embrace in the park.

"I... I'm a Devil?" Issei muttered, the fear slowly being overshadowed by his overwhelming teenage hormones. "And I serve you, President? A beautiful, high-class Devil?" A goofy, entirely inappropriate grin began to spread across his face. "Honestly, that sounds like an absolute win!"

Rias blinked, slightly taken aback by his rapid, hormonally driven acceptance, before a small, amused smile touched her lips. "I am glad you are adaptable, Issei."

Instantly, the ambient temperature in the room dropped. Rias’s smile vanished, replaced by the cold, uncompromising gaze of a monarch defending her territory. She shifted her attention to the two brothers standing casually beside the newly minted Devil.

Ren was still wearing his thick black blindfold, his hands resting in his pockets, while Ariel stood with his arms crossed, the heavy iron weights beneath his uniform clanking softly as he shifted his stance.

"Now," Rias said, her voice dropping an octave. "Let us address the anomalies. Ariel Veritas. Ren Veritas. My first and most pressing question: What are your intentions in Kuoh Town? Are you agents of a rival faction sent to interfere with my territory, and should the Underworld consider you a threat?"

Ariel and Ren exchanged a brief, entirely relaxed look, though Ren’s was obscured by his blindfold.

"President Gremory," Ariel started, flashing a bright, disarming grin. "We are literally just here to hang out with Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama. We have zero hostile intentions toward you, your peerage, or the Underworld. We don't care about factional politics. In fact, since Issei is part of your club now, you can consider us entirely supportive of the ORC."

Ren nodded in agreement, his tone perfectly level. "If our presence inherently triggers your territorial defense protocols, we are willing to submit to voluntary containment. We can wear demonic monitoring devices, or you may physically tie us to these chairs to verify our compliance. We have no desire to incite paranoia."

The absolute sincerity of their offer—and the casual willingness to be tied up—completely shattered the dramatic tension Rias had been trying to build. Akeno brought a hand to her mouth, stifling a surprised giggle, while Kiba coughed awkwardly into his fist.

"That... will not be necessary," Rias said, slightly flustered. She quickly regained her composure. "But that brings us to the next mystery. Koneko’s senjutsu and Kiba’s magical scans confirm you possess absolutely zero demonic, angelic, or divine energy. You are biologically mundane. Yet, Ren deflected a weapon of light with a standard carbon-steel knife, and Ariel crushed a superheated light spear with his bare palm. If you are not affiliated with the Three Factions, what exactly *are* you?"

"And what did you mean by having your 'limiters' removed?" Kiba added, his eyes burning with a swordsman’s intense curiosity.

"We are human," Ren answered calmly, tilting his blindfolded head toward the Knight. "Nothing more. The issue is that modern humanity has fundamentally forgotten what that entails. Society today dismisses sensory honing, internal energy cultivation, and extreme biological conditioning as myth, choosing instead to rely solely on basic physical fitness and superficial fighting techniques. We simply pushed human martial arts and internal energy cultivation to their absolute, logical extremes."

"Exactly," Ariel chimed in, flexing a bicep. "Any human could technically achieve what we do if they trained hard enough. Those 'limiters' you heard us mention were just highly dense, internal training weights we placed on our own energy pathways to make daily life more challenging. Taking them off just let us access our full, cultivated human potential."

Rias and her peerage stared at them in profound disbelief. The idea that pure, unadulterated human martial arts could bridge the gap to the supernatural was fundamentally alien to them.

"Fascinating," Akeno murmured, her eyes glittering. "But that does not explain your knowledge. You knew Issei possessed the President's flyer, and you deliberately abandoned him to save your other friends because you knew we would resurrect him. How do you know so much about our operations?"

"Our sensory training isn't just physical," Ren explained smoothly. "We cultivate our awareness to sense intentions, biological rhythms, and non-human signatures. We were aware that Issei was carrying an anomalous magical artifact. We were also fully aware that your Rook, Koneko, was monitoring Issei for days."

Ren turned his head precisely toward where Koneko was sitting. "For example, she was sitting on the branch of the cherry blossom tree observing us when Issei was attempting to peek at the Kendo club last Thursday."

Koneko paused mid-bite of her chocolate bar, her golden eyes widening in genuine, uncharacteristic shock. A faint blush dusted her cheeks as she realized these "humans" had easily detected her espionage.

"As for our deeper knowledge of your world," Ren continued, his voice taking on a slightly more serious, rhythmic tone. "We possess a promise to fulfill regarding the Occult Research Club. It is a vow that binds us to your future. However, we cannot explain the exact parameters of this promise yet. We ask that you wait exactly one month. After the conclusion of the upcoming Rating Game incident—the Riser Phenex affair—we will reveal everything."

Rias flinched visibly. The mention of Riser Phenex—a deeply guarded, highly personal political nightmare she had kept entirely hidden from her peerage—proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that these brothers possessed information they had absolutely no right to know.

"The third boy," Koneko suddenly spoke up, her voice regaining its stoic edge. "The one who utilized Future Sight. Who is he? What is the 'Infinite Reality' he returned to?"

"Ah, Fajar," Ariel laughed warmly. "He's a comrade in arms. He's the founder of our little 'fiction to reality' community. We basically took concepts like internal cultivation, advanced haki, and dimensional physics that normal people dismiss as fiction, and proved they weren't myths. Fajar is currently in his own realm. Explaining the mechanics of his existence right now would just give you all a massive headache. Like Ren said, we ask for your patience until next month."

The room fell silent as Rias processed the overwhelming, paradigm-shifting information. These were not enemies. They were anomalous, impossibly strong humans who treated supernatural threats like sparring partners, yet they possessed a baffling, respectful loyalty to Issei, Matsuda, and Motohama.

Slowly, the icy, regal facade of the Crimson-Haired Ruin Princess melted away. Rias sighed, her shoulders relaxing as a genuinely warm, kind smile spread across her face. The imposing monarch vanished, replaced by a caring, deeply empathetic young woman.

"I want to make something perfectly clear to both of you," Rias said softly, looking between Ariel and Ren. "I hold absolutely no prejudice against humans. The Occult Research Club is a sanctuary, and I have no problem whatsoever with humans joining us or associating with my peerage. My hostility earlier was not born of arrogance."

Rias glanced toward the window, her expression tightening with genuine worry. "It was born of fear. The supernatural world is unimaginably dangerous. My primary duty as a King is to protect my servants. When humans get involved with us, they inevitably become targets. And frankly, baseline humans are fragile. They cannot protect themselves. If you join our circle, it endangers my peerage, because we would be forced to constantly divide our attention to keep you alive."

She turned her gaze back to them, her eyes full of sorrowful concern. "I am not worried about the two of you anymore. You have proven you can dismantle a Fallen Angel strike team with terrifying ease. But Matsuda and Motohama are truly, entirely mundane. They survived by sheer luck yesterday. If they continue to associate with Issei, they will be targeted again. And I cannot guarantee their safety."

Ariel’s grin softened into a look of absolute, unshakable resolve. He stepped forward, the iron weights clanking decisively.

"You don't have to guarantee their safety, President," Ariel said, his voice carrying the immovable weight of a mountain. "We will."

Ren adjusted his posture, his multiversal presence bleeding just slightly into the room—a warm, protective aura that felt fundamentally different from demonic magic. "Issei has the Gremory clan to protect him. We will take full, absolute responsibility for Matsuda and Motohama. If any supernatural entity, regardless of their faction, attempts to harm them, we will handle it personally. You do not need to divide your forces to protect our friends."

The heavy, lingering anxiety in the clubroom evaporated instantly. Rias’s eyes widened, touched by the sheer, unwavering loyalty these anomalously powerful humans possessed. Kiba smiled genuinely, recognizing the pure chivalry in their declaration, while Akeno let out a soft, approving hum.

"Very well," Rias said, her warm smile returning in full force. She extended her hand across the desk. "Ariel Veritas. Ren Veritas. We accept your terms, and we look forward to the revelations you promised next month. Until then, you are officially welcome in the Occult Research Club territory as esteemed friends."
